defects.proposedCure: Consume `useSliderAnnouncements` (or the `sliderAnnouncement` formatter beneath it) from ConfigSliderPane, fed the same `fmt()` cell the row already renders — ONE voice, no second formatter.

defects.defect: `read()` casts `readPath`'s honest `undefined` to `number`, and `fmt()` then calls `.toFixed` on it during RENDER — one absent optional branch unmounts the entire pane through the error boundary, and the boundary swallows the failure so no pageerror or console noise is emitted. `writePath` has the mirror hole (`Cannot set properties of undefined`).
defects.evidence: ConfigSliderPane.vue:57-73 (writePath, three unchecked casts), :76-78 (`return readPath(config, key) as number` — the lie), :84-86 (fmt). Pass-1 injection on /#/atmosphere with the type-legal state `config.zones = undefined`: pane replaced by 'This panel hit an unexpected error. Cannot read properties of undefined (reading toFixed)', `configConsoleStillMounted: false`, `rowsAfter: 0`, and crucially `pageErrors: []`, `consoleNoise: []` — which is why REPORT.json shows 0 console/page errors on both routes in all four matrices. The tell is internal: AuroraPane guards the SAME key three lines away (`atoms.zones?.arrangement ?? 'composed'` :74, `atoms.zones?.count ?? 4` :82) while its slider def `{key:'zones.count'}` :103 does not.
defects.mechanism: A stringly-typed reflection layer whose type signature asserts a totality the implementation does not have; BlobPane buys a 13-line NumericAtomPath mapped type to guard the key literals while the object it indexes is double-cast to `Record<string, unknown>` and fully untyped.
defects.reproduction: Pass-1 probe injected `config.zones = undefined` on the live reactive object at /#/atmosphere. Mechanism alone: `node -e "const f=v=>Number.isInteger(v)?String(v):v.toFixed(3); f(undefined)"` throws. Reachability through the UI today is a HYPOTHESIS — all three aurora keys resolve at boot.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the reflection layer. Give `SliderDef` its own typed lens (`get: () => number` / `set: (n:number) => void`), or make it generic over the config shape (`SliderDef<C> { key: NumericPath<C> }` with `ConfigSliderPane<C extends object>`). That deletes readPath/writePath, the `as number` lie, BlobPane's 13-line local mapped type, and both `(x as unknown) as Record<string, unknown>` call-site casts — strictly less code.

defects.defect: (a) 31 `<label>` elements that label nothing — no `for`, no `id`, wrapping no control — so clicking a row's label neither focuses nor moves its slider; the name is duplicated onto the thumb via aria-label instead of wiring the label that exists. (b) 7 visually grouped sections with ZERO programmatic grouping: bare `<span>` titles, no role=group, no fieldset, no heading — 31 sliders in one undifferentiated run to assistive tech (WCAG 1.3.1).
defects.evidence: Measured: `labelCount: 31, labelsWithFor: 0` on /#/blob (3/0 on /#/atmosphere); pass-1 `labelsWrappingControl: 0`, `groupOrHeading: 0`, AX tree contains exactly two headings, both outside the console. ConfigSliderPane.vue:128-130 renders section titles as `<span class="config-section-title">`. The producer NAMES the right primitive: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/configurator/ConfiguratorRow.vue.d.ts:41-47 — 'ConfiguratorRow … No a11y for/id wiring … use LabeledField directly for an accessible form control, including inside a Configurator. Reach for ConfiguratorRow only when token metadata or reset is the content.'
defects.mechanism: A token/preset row primitive used for 31 real form controls, against its own documented advice, with aria-label papering over the hole.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/blob → click any slider's visible label text; nothing focuses. Or: `document.querySelectorAll('.config-console .configurator-row label[for]').length === 0`.
defects.proposedCure: Use `LabeledField` — the producer names it, it ships, and it does the for/id/aria-describedby wiring. For grouping, the section wrapper (:123-127) becomes `role="group" :aria-labelledby="sectionId"` with the title span carrying that id — two attributes, no new markup, no new component.

The style block simultaneously asserts a '≥44px touch rung' it does not deliver on the width axis.

defects.defect: Two of the three most heavily justified CSS cures in the file are provably inert. (a) `min-block-size: clamp(2rem, 7cqi, 2.625rem)` on .configurator-row — its MAXIMUM is 42px while rows measure 61px desktop / 77.6px coarse, so it never binds. (b) The `@media (pointer: coarse)` ::before hit extension adds exactly 0px, because a producer utility already sets the same 44px.
defects.evidence: ConfigSliderPane.vue:208-217 (clamp), :218-230 (::before). (a) measured `rowH 61` at 1440 vs 42px ceiling; `rowH 77.6` with computed `min-block-size: 32px` at 430. (b) ABLATION (scratchpad/cspane-probe3.mjs): injecting `…glass-slider::before{display:none!important}` gives `rootH: 44, rootHNoBefore: 44`; `beforeBlock "44px"` = 100%. ATTRIBUTION (cspane-probe4.mjs, CDP CSS.getMatchedStylesForNode filtered to min-block-size) returns exactly one rule: `{selector: "[data-control-target]", media: "(pointer: coarse)", css: "min-block-size: var(--touch-target, 2.75rem); min-inline-size: …"}` = node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/utilities/responsive.css:1, and .glass-slider already carries data-control-target (slider-DzqeQmMu.js). glass-ui ships NO coarse rule for .glass-slider itself (three coarse blocks in glass-ui.css: tags-input, continuous-dot, segmented-dot).
defects.mechanism: 13 lines of :deep() CSS reaching into a design-system primitive to re-implement a utility the design system already applies app-wide; and a clamp whose ceiling sits below the row's intrinsic content height. Both carry live prose claims the next reader will trust.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/cspane-probe3.mjs (ablation) and cspane-probe4.mjs (CDP attribution).
defects.proposedCure: Delete both blocks. If a rhythm is genuinely wanted, make it a real `block-size`, not a `min-block-size` under the content height. Violates edict 3 (no contrivance) and edict 5 (never per-instance override the design-system root).

defects.defect: The file's own header states it composes glass-ui's ./configurator surface, then composes the ROW and rebuilds the STATE by hand: `Record<string, unknown>` + readPath/writePath + a bare unguarded `Object.assign(config, structuredClone(defaults))` with no try/catch, no isDirty, and no per-row reset — while ConfiguratorRow ships `canReset` + a `reset` emit + an auto-generated `aria-label="Reset {label}"` that the pane passes neither of, so the only reset is nuclear.
defects.evidence: ConfigSliderPane.vue:6-10 (the stated principle) vs :92-94 (the hand-roll). Producer offers useConfiguratorState<T extends object> with typed config, resetCurrent(), isDirty, and an explicit `clone` hook whose structuredClone call is try/caught with a diagnostic (configurator-M5OaIlJd.js fn `ce`); its reset semantics are a FULL REPLACE (fn `m`: delete keys absent from target, then assign) — a third, different contract from the demo's shallow merge. Unguarded clone is latent, not live: `node -e "import {reactive} from 'vue'; structuredClone(reactive({a:1,n:{b:2}}))"` → DataCloneError, but both consumers today pass plain module constants (proved cloneable by useAtmosphere.ts:128,381).
defects.mechanism: Edict 4 met on the row axis and unmet on the state axis — the still-open C10 A4 [P1] book.
defects.reproduction: Code read; the DataCloneError one-liner above demonstrates the latent path.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt useConfiguratorState<T> (C10 A4 [P1], docs/tranches/N/audit/lanes/C10.md:92-105, :265), or at minimum consume ConfiguratorRow's canReset/reset for per-row restore. Either way the reset domain must become the declared domain (D-1).

defects.defect: VACUOUS GATE — no test in the repository exercises a single behaviour of this file. The only coverage is two e2e colour-contrast oracles that read computed colours and never move a slider, press a button, or read a value; o7-card-census explicitly EXCLUDES the pane with a grep standing in for the runtime walk.
defects.evidence: `ls -R demo/test` → export/byte-exact.test.ts, glass/aurora-bracket.test.ts, glass/aurora-motion.test.ts (the latter two assert DEFAULT_AURORA_ATOMS constants + resolveAtoms; neither imports the pane). e2e/smoke/oracles/o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:924 and :1161 assert ratio only. e2e/smoke/oracles/o7-card-census.spec.ts:38-42 excludes it by name. 19 vitest files in test/: zero mention. Green-keeping mutations: M1 `update(){}` (all 34 sliders read-only), M2 `resetDefaults(){}`, M3 `copyAsJson(){}`, M4 `fmt(){return "0"}`, and NEW M5 — delete `:aria-label="def.label"` at :145, removing the 31 sliders' ONLY accessible name, and o18 still passes because it samples the orphan <label> (D-6a) which is not the control's accessible name.
defects.mechanism: The gate measures pixels of an element no assistive technology associates with the control, so it can be green, honest about what it samples, and still certify nothing about behaviour. This is what let three waves of inert cures accumulate (D-3, D-7, D-8, D-11a, D-15).
defects.reproduction: Apply any of M1–M5 and run the suite: `npx vitest run && npx playwright test` — GREEN.
defects.proposedCure: Five small mounted vitest cases: dot-path round-trip (flat AND nested); resetDefaults preserving a declared live key at depth 2 (D-1's exact assertion); copy payload equalling the declared projection (D-14's exact assertion); fmt at {0,-0,NaN,Infinity,undefined} and at each declared step (D-15); the clipboard Result on both reason values. Fix this FIRST — it kills M1–M5 and makes the next inert cure impossible to land.

defects.defect: NEW in this pass. `fmt()` ignores the declared `SliderDef.step` and formats by a heuristic on the VALUE, so the readout changes shape as the value moves: knobs sitting at exactly 0 render "0" beside neighbours rendering three decimals, and dragging any knob whose domain contains 0 makes the readout jump 5 glyphs → 1 → 5 inside a `truncate` inline row.
defects.evidence: ConfigSliderPane.vue:84-86 — `Number.isInteger(v) ? String(v) : v.toFixed(3)`; `def.step` declared at :31 and never read. BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS.color.satShift === 0 and .brightnessShift === 0 (verified against the dist), so both render "0" while measured live neighbours render `Body Radius 0.220`, `Sat Radius 0.082`, `Orbit Radius 0.170`, `Eccentricity 0.050`, `Smooth K 0.050`. Same for Warp, Noise Amp, Pulse Amp, Attraction. Conversely a step-100 knob is "2500" only because the value is incidentally integral.
defects.mechanism: Precision decided by value shape rather than by the control's declared resolution — the declaration is right there on the SliderDef and is unused.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/blob → scroll to Color → Saturation reads "0" while every sibling reads three decimals; drag it one step either way and watch the readout width jump.
defects.proposedCure: `const dp = Math.max(0, -Math.floor(Math.log10(def.step))); v.toFixed(dp)`. Precision then always equals what the control can express and the readout width is constant across the whole domain — one line, and it deletes the heuristic rather than tuning it.

defects.defect: Dead branches, a false JSDoc, and prop mutation. (a) :44 documents 'Pass empty array to show empty state' — there is no empty state; :119 and :163 both gate on `sections.length > 0` and with [] the pane renders a bare header, and no consumer ever passes empty, so both guards are permanently-true dead branches protecting a nonexistent state. (b) The child mutates the object handed down as a prop (:80-82) while aurora-atoms.ts:11 names the house idiom as 'the demo's standing injection-key-over-prop-drill idiom'. (c) `read(): number` casts an unknown that is provably sometimes undefined.
defects.evidence: ConfigSliderPane.vue:44 vs :119/:163; :80-82 (writePath into `config`); :76-78. Both consumers double-cast their typed config to nothing purely so the child can mutate it: `:config="(cfg as unknown) as Record<string, unknown>"` (BlobPane.vue:124, AuroraPane.vue:111). Measured sectionsLen: 7 (blob) / 1 (aurora) — never 0.
defects.mechanism: Prose asserting behaviour the code does not have (edict 2 family: dead surface), plus a one-way-data-flow inversion that exists only because the reflection layer needs a mutable bag.
defects.reproduction: Code read; `sections: []` renders header + slot and nothing else.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the JSDoc clause and both dead guards, or build the empty state. For (b): have ConfigSliderPane take a `configKey: InjectionKey<T>` and own its own inject — which also deletes both `as unknown as` double-casts at the call sites. (c) is cured by D-5's typed lens.

defects.defect: HYPOTHESIS TESTED AND DISPROVED — the per-render fan-out (read(def.key) evaluated twice per row plus a fresh [read(key)] array literal per row, all inside the render function) is NOT a performance defect.
defects.evidence: scratchpad/cspane-probe2.mjs §B — 200 synthetic ArrowRight keydowns back-to-back, settled across two rAFs, median of five: `{route:'atmosphere', rows:3, medianMs:71.1, perPressMs:0.3555}` vs `{route:'blob', rows:31, medianMs:72.5, perPressMs:0.3625}` → ratio 1.02x across a 10x row count. Pass 1's dispatch→first-MutationObserver latency (6.675ms blob vs 5.463ms atmosphere, +22%) is consistent, not contradictory — it includes one full paint; the marginal per-row render work is ~43us and below the noise floor when coalesced. Pass-1 mutationFanout confirms Vue's patch is correct: one keystroke mutates exactly one row's DOM (mutatedRows [0] of 31).
defects.mechanism: n/a — recorded as negative proof so no seat promotes it without a number and no seat re-chases it a third time.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/cspane-probe2.mjs
defects.proposedCure: None required. Do not 'optimise' this; the shape is fine and the cost is elsewhere in the app.

result.strongestDefect: D-1 taken together with its twin D-14. `resetDefaults()` (ConfigSliderPane.vue:92-94) is a depth-1 `Object.assign` over an object whose depth-2 members are externally owned, so one click on Reset silently destroys the picker-derived blob palette with no undo and no visible symptom — reproduced through the PUBLIC UI only (Copy JSON → Reset → Copy JSON, no Vue internals touched): `["#ffbde0","#ffdde5","#fff6f6","#fff6f4"]` → `["#b5947f","#d4b27d","#dad6b1"]`, byte-identical across two independent audit passes a session apart. D-14 is why it reaches the user: `copyAsJson` stringifies the whole proxy, so the corrupted state — and, on the aurora side, the live picked colour `"seed":"lab(92% 88.8 20)"` that DEFAULT_AURORA_ATOMS deliberately omits — goes straight to the clipboard. Both fall out of the same root: the component manipulates "the config" as an opaque bag while its own `sections` prop is sitting right there already declaring exactly which keys it owns. Reset guesses; Copy guesses wider. The cure is to stop guessing — derive read, write, reset and copy from the one declaration the component already has.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this field carries the disproved hypotheses instead — recorded so no seat re-chases them. (1) PERFORMANCE: per-keystroke cost 0.3555 ms at 3 rows vs 0.3625 ms at 31 rows = 1.02x across a 10x row count (cspane-probe2.mjs, 200 dispatches x5, median) — the double read() and per-row array allocation are below the noise floor; NOT a defect. (2) DOMAIN BOUNDARIES: Home → aria-valuenow 0.08 / readout "0.080"; End → 0.45 / "0.450"; pageerrors []. Sound at both bounds, step honoured. (3) structuredClone throwing: both `defaults` are plain module constants, proved cloneable by useAtmosphere.ts:128 and :381 cloning the same two objects at boot — latent (a reactive defaults would DataCloneError), not live. (4) NAMELESS BUTTONS = 0 contributed: REPORT.md records /#/blob:1 but /#/atmosphere:0 across all four Safari matrices while rendering the identical ConfigSliderPane chrome; the pane's own two buttons measure 134.9x36 and 89x36, both text-labelled and >=24px. (5) READOUT TRUNCATION: readoutsTruncated 0 on both routes at 1440x900 despite ConfiguratorRow applying `truncate`. (6) THE REPO'S NAMED LOCAL HAZARDS ARE ALL ABSENT: no defineModel (no async round-trip stale read), no oklch→HSV roundtrip/stableHue, no ValueUnit construction, no parseCssColor, no canvas/WebGL, and ZERO requestAnimationFrame / setTimeout / setInterval / addEventListener / observers — nothing to leak, and the PRM-RAF epidemic does not touch this file (all 95 script lines read). (7) EDICT 8 satisfied — this file imports only values; both consumers use `import type`. (8) `--slider-track-bg` at :202 is NOT an edict-5 violation: it is a producer-supported token (glass-ui.css `.slider-track{background:var(--slider-track-bg,…)}`); the edict-5 violations are the other three :deep() rules (:204, :215, :219-229).

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for demo/scenes/about/markdown/Markdown.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id claude-opus-5[1m], the tier declared at spawn. Declared, not inherited. No defect on this axis.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — the demo module lattice is documentation, not law: eslint.config.js:232-238 keys its three no-restricted-imports objects on the demo/@ tree W43 deleted, so `eslint --print-config demo/scenes/about/markdown/Markdown.vue` returns no-restricted-imports UNSET for the subject and its composables, while only the library's inv-K-1 survives; strictTemplates is absent from every tsconfig. This is the enabling condition — every other finding is something a live lattice would have refused. Independently re-verified by this seat.
result.negativeProof: The single axis of the challenge premise that comes back clean is the published-surface consumption, and it comes back clean structurally rather than by luck. vite.config.ts:41-50 GENERATES the resolve.alias set by iterating package.json#exports and mapping each key to conditions.import (dist/subpaths/*.js), so useMarkdownColors.ts:3-4 (`import { convertColor } from "@mkbabb/value.js/color"` / `import { parseCssColor } from "@mkbabb/value.js/css"`) resolves through the real published artifact. Verified: both are real exports keys (`grep -n 'convertColor' src/subpaths/color.ts` → :16; `grep -n 'parseCssColor' src/subpaths/css.ts` → :47), and no deep src/ import exists anywhere in demo/. A real npm consumer could write those two lines verbatim — this is dogfooding, not a false proof of the public API. Also proved negative by measurement: (a) the brief's named suspect "three parallel useDark stores at useMarkdownHighlighting.ts:76" is CURED — line 76 is the comment describing the landed cure; all call sites are useGlobalDark from @mkbabb/glass-ui/dark, zero vueuse useDark. (b) No duplicate markdown renderer exists — one component, one consumer (AboutPane.vue:50). (c) demo/ui/alert and demo/ui/skeleton are genuine glass-ui re-exports, not local re-implementations — the shim TREE is the defect, duplicated logic is not. (d) verbatimModuleSyntax satisfied: Markdown.vue:40 and useMarkdownHighlighting.ts:1 both use `import type`. (e) ref() on a dynamic-import namespace does NOT deep-proxy — measured Object.isExtensible(ns)===false, isReactive(ref(ns).value)===false — so today's call site is safe (see L-16 for why that safety is unstated rather than structural).

defects.defect: The demo module lattice is unenforced by construction: eslint.config.js's three no-restricted-imports objects are keyed on the deleted demo/@ tree, and the subject component plus its composables are governed by no import rule whatsoever. strictTemplates is off everywhere, so unknown component props are never reported.

defects.mechanism: An enforcement layer left pointing at a tree that was renamed out from under it (W43/RF-15 killed demo/@), never re-keyed and never re-measured. Vacuous twice over: no file matches the files glob, and no import could match the banned @-alias patterns since tsconfig.demo.json:32-34 records every project alias was killed.
defects.reproduction: The three commands in the evidence field, run at c654824e on branch tranche-u. Independently reproduced by this seat (Revision 3).
defects.proposedCure: Re-key the three objects onto the real tree (demo/{color-session,palettes,picker,platform,scenes,shared,shell,ui,workbenches}/**) and state the lattice as relative-depth bans — a scene leaf may not climb out of its scene (../../../../), a feature may not import from color-picker/ (the boot shell). Enable vueCompilerOptions.strictTemplates, which turns L-7 into a compile error. Both are mechanically verifiable and need no design ruling. This is a repo-wide rider, not this component's wave, and it should land FIRST among the riders — it is the only finding that prevents the others from returning.

The component holds BOTH spellings of the same intent four lines apart: the runtime `import` at :37-38 (wrong) and the Tailwind-4 compile-time `@reference` at :79 (correct, emits nothing). Revision 2 graded this MINOR because 'Vite dedupes by id'; but the harmlessness is contingent on a co-incidence at ANOTHER file (App.vue happening to import the same ids), and Revision 2 names the trigger itself — delete App.vue:199-200 and 514 KiB silently relocates into the lazy About chunk. defects.defect: The single class name coupling this component to the build pipeline — .markdown-body — is an undeclared default of a floating third-party dependency range, owned by neither the component nor the repo, with four in-repo dependents not one of which can report its own absence.
defects.evidence: Producer: `grep -n 'Markdown(' vite.config.ts` → "162: Markdown({})," (zero options); `grep -n 'wrapperClasses: "markdown-body"' node_modules/unplugin-vue-markdown/dist/src-5Xwh9b7i.mjs` → :281; types-CAs0WWKP.d.mts:166 "@default 'markdown-body'" with a sibling `wrapperDiv?: boolean` that makes the class vanish entirely when false; package.json devDependencies → unplugin-vue-markdown ^32.0.0 (floating minor). Four consumers, all silent on failure: Markdown.vue:98 (compiles to `.markdown-body[data-v-b622b24b]`), Markdown.vue:104 and :198 (both compile to `.markdown-wrapper[data-v-b622b24b] .markdown-body` — emitted TWICE, verified by json-decoding __vite__css from the dev server's scoped-style module: 10246 bytes, three selectors, two identical), and useMarkdownHighlighting.ts:11 `container.querySelector(".markdown-body")` guarded by `:12 if (!body) return;`.
defects.mechanism: An abstention from declaring a contract. Markdown({}) is not a neutral call — the feature stands on an upstream default under a caret range, so an upstream minor can retire it and the repo's response would be ~100 dead typography rules plus vanished colour-space marking, with green CI. Compounding it, two mechanisms serve one concept: site 1 relies on Vue propagating the parent's scope id onto a CHILD COMPONENT's root element; sites 2-3 rely on ordinary descendant matching. Site 1 additionally dies if the .md wrapper ever renders a fragment or wrapperDiv:false is set — the identical silent-dead-rule failure class the SFC's own comment at :81-97 documents having already suffered once for the inner elements. The cure landed for the inner elements and left the root on the old mechanism.
defects.reproduction: The four greps and the compiled-CSS decode in the evidence field are fully reproduced. The BREAKAGE is a hypothesis — this seat may not edit source, so I did not stage an upstream bump; the failure is proved by mechanism and by the `if (!body) return;` early-out at useMarkdownHighlighting.ts:12, not by observed regression.
defects.proposedCure: Immediate, one line, and the same line that cures L-4: `Markdown({ wrapperClasses: "markdown-body" })` at vite.config.ts:162 — declare the seam the repo actually depends on. Architecturally better: under the greenfield lattice the seam disappears rather than being declared — the stylesheet moves to demo/styles/prose.css keyed on a class the repo owns, and markSpaceName.ts receives the container element from useTemplateRef instead of re-finding it by string. A concept that no longer needs a name shared across a package boundary cannot drift across one. Lands inside wave MD-a; closing evidence `grep -c 'wrapperClasses' vite.config.ts` = 1.

defects.defect: useMarkdownColors is a hand copy of useSafeAccentFn("resting"), assembled from a 4-hop reach into three separate color-session files, and it omits the epoch-bump the canonical composable encapsulates. A color-session export (resolveSurfaceLightnessLive) exists only to enable the copy, and its own docstring names this component as the beneficiary.
defects.evidence: Canonical: demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:345-362 useSafeAccentFn = useGlobalDark + inject(INK_AMBIENT_KEY) + bumpProbeEpochOnMount() + certifyAccentInk(css, surfaceLightnessNow(surface, ambient, isDark), floor). The copy: useMarkdownColors.ts:5-7 imports INK_AMBIENT_KEY, certifyAccentInk, resolveSurfaceLightnessLive from three files; :18 useGlobalDark, :25 inject(INK_AMBIENT_KEY), :44 resolveSurfaceLightnessLive("resting", ambient.value, isDark.value), :70 certifyAccentInk — identical recipe, bumpProbeEpochOnMount ABSENT. The enabler: useContrastSafeColor.ts:370-376 is a one-line pass-through to the private surfaceLightnessNow, whose docstring (:364-369) reads "for composables that fold the referent into their own computation (`useMarkdownColors`)". The contract it violates is stated in law-voice at :69-77: a folding consumer "must register the mount bump from its setup, or its first (possibly detached/pre-style) probe result caches until some OTHER consumer happens to bump the epoch." Census: `grep -rn bumpProbeEpochOnMount demo/` → ConsoleRail.vue:133 yes, useViewAccents.ts:89 yes, useMarkdownColors.ts ABSENT, HeroBlob.vue:99 ABSENT — 2 of 4 external folders violate it. Second half: certifyAccentInk treats an unparseable colour as benign (ink.ts:136 `if (!accent) return css;`) while useMarkdownColors.ts:33/37/41 THROWS from inside a computed the template reads via :style="mdColorVars", on a value driven by the live picked colour.
defects.mechanism: Ownership duplication — one concept, two homes, and the copy loses the encapsulated obligation. The escape-hatch export is the tell: a pure alias for a private function, minted so call sites can re-implement the composable beside it, then broadened to four consumers. The stated justification does not even hold for the consumer it was minted for — useMarkdownColors DOES certify a whole colour through certifyAccentInk, the identical call safeCss makes with identical arguments. Also one concept with two failure policies, the stricter one wired to render.
defects.reproduction: The greps and file:line reads above are fully reproduced (verified by this seat in Revision 3). The SYMPTOM is NOT reproduced and is labelled a hypothesis: in the live app the boot writer's useContrastSafeColor bumps the epoch at App mount, which self-heals the first read; I did not observe a wrong paint. The contract violation is proven; the wrong-contrast consequence is not.
defects.proposedCure: Replace the quartet with `const { safeCss } = useSafeAccentFn("resting"); const accent = safeCss(`oklch(${L} ${headingC} ${headingH})`);` — 3 deep imports collapse to 1, and mdColorVars returns {} on unparseable input so inherited ink stands instead of a render-path throw. Then DELETE resolveSurfaceLightnessLive and migrate HeroBlob.vue:99, ConsoleRail.vue:136 and useViewAccents.ts:108 the same way: the epoch bump becomes structurally impossible to omit because there is nothing left to omit. Wave MD-c.

defects.evidence: Composition measured: total 408 lines, style 331 (81.1%), script+template 77 (18.9%). DOM census (headless Chromium against :9000): wrapperDataV ["data-v-b622b24b"], bodyDataV ["data-v-b622b24b"], h2DataV [] — no content element carries the scope attribute. Compiled CSS decoded from the dev server's scoped-style module (10246 bytes) contains exactly three markdown selectors: `.markdown-body[data-v-b622b24b]` once, `.markdown-wrapper[data-v-b622b24b] .markdown-body` TWICE (SFC lines 104 and 198). The block's own comment at :94-96 claims the --phi-* rungs "live in style.css :root" — `find demo -name style.css` returns nothing; they are at foundation.css:458-462.
defects.mechanism: SFC-local styling used as the home for a design-system concern; :deep() normalised from rare exception into permanent posture. The file's comment at :81-97 presents the universal :deep() routing as a CURE — it is the diagnosis. Ownership check performed: glass-ui 7.0.0 exports 73 subpaths and none is prose/typography/markdown, and the phi ladder plus --md-color-* are value.js-doc-specific, so edict 4 is satisfied by a demo style layer at the same tier as the existing animations.css / utils.css / hljs.css. defects.reproduction: The awk composition measurement and the compiled-CSS decode are reproduced by this seat; the DOM census is Revision 2's, carried forward.
defects.proposedCure: Extract the block verbatim to demo/styles/prose.css, wired at foundation.css:82 beside the hljs precedent. Every :deep() disappears, the arbitrary 104/198 split heals, L-9's rogue imports go with it, and the component drops 408 -> ~77 lines without altering one rendered pixel. Wave MD-a; closing evidence `grep -c ':deep(' Markdown.vue` = 0 plus a byte-identical computed-style diff on h2 colour/family/margin-top.

defects.defect: The doc registry lives in the consumer, the content lives outside demo/, and the edge between them is a directory-level dependency cycle. The colour-space domain is enumerated twice, with a load-bearing cast proving the two are not known to agree.
defects.evidence: AboutPane.vue:79 `type MarkdownSpace = "rgb"|"hex"|...|"kelvin"` hand-copies DisplayColorSpace (demo/color-session/color-model.ts:31); :81-93 holds the 11-entry registry as `() => import("../../../assets/docs/rgb.md")`; :97 casts `as MarkdownSpace`. The cycle: AboutPane.vue:82 -> assets/docs/*.md (repo-root sibling of demo/), and `grep -rn 'import .* from' assets/docs/*.md` → all 11 files line 2 `import { Katex } from "../../demo/scenes/about/katex";`. Those .md files are compiled as Vue SFCs (vite.config.ts:161 `Vue({ include: [/\.vue$/, /\.md$/] })`; assets/docs/lab.md:1 is `<script setup>` — confirmed by fetching it from the dev server).
defects.mechanism: Split ownership plus an inverted edge. The markdown/ module owns the TYPE of a doc loader but cannot resolve its own content, so its single consumer must hand it one — the indirection buys nothing and costs the registry its home. Meanwhile 11 demo components live outside demo/ and import back into demo/scenes/about/, making the content un-relocatable: moving scenes/about/katex/ breaks 11 files outside the app tree. And the parallel enumeration fails silently — add a space to DisplayColorSpace and the lookup returns undefined, the v-if at AboutPane.vue:51 hides the guide, nothing errors.
defects.reproduction: The greps above, fully reproduced by this seat (the 11-way assets/docs -> demo/scenes/about/katex edge independently confirmed).
defects.proposedCure: Move assets/docs/ -> demo/scenes/about/docs/ (they are demo components; nothing else reads them); the Katex import becomes "../katex" — one hop, no inversion — and assets/ is removed entirely. Move the registry behind the module seam keyed off the canonical union: `export const colorSpaceDocs: Record<DisplayColorSpace, () => Promise<Component>>`. Record<DisplayColorSpace,...> is exhaustive by construction, so a new space becomes a compile error and the `as` cast dies. Wave MD-d.

defects.defect: The component calls a glass-ui API that does not exist: <Skeleton surface="glass" variant="shimmer"> passes two undeclared props that fall through onto the root as inert HTML attributes, and nothing in the toolchain can catch it.
defects.evidence: Markdown.vue:4,6,7 pass surface and variant. glass-ui 7.0.0's Skeleton declares exactly one prop — verified independently by this seat at node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/skeleton/Skeleton.vue.d.ts: `type __VLS_Props = { class?: HTMLAttributes["class"] };`. Nothing catches it because strictTemplates is unset everywhere (L-1).
defects.mechanism: A design intent expressed through an API that was never implemented. It LOOKS right only because shimmer is glass-ui's unconditional default — the props would keep 'working' if glass-ui changed it. Second-order and more interesting: glass-ui's skeleton fills with var(--muted), while this component's own style block at :229-232 rules that content chips seat on --well-bg, "never the parallel --muted species (which stepped OPPOSITE the well in dark)." The skeleton it ships sits on precisely the banned tone, and the component believes it already cured that via props that do not exist.
defects.reproduction: The .d.ts read above, independently reproduced by this seat.
defects.proposedCure: Per edict 4 the fix belongs in glass-ui as a real Skeleton variant, relayed to the active glass-ui BH inbox per the standing relay edict — not a demo-side override. Enabling vueCompilerOptions.strictTemplates (L-1) makes this class of defect a compile error rather than a silent no-op. Rider, not this component's wave.

defects.defect: demo/ui/ is a 19-directory back-compat shim tree by its own written admission, and both spellings of the same import are live simultaneously across the demo. The subject routes two of its four value-carrying imports through it.
defects.evidence: Markdown.vue:35-36 import from ../../../ui/alert and ../../../ui/skeleton. Census: all 19 demo/ui/* dirs are single-file pure pass-throughs to @mkbabb/glass-ui (18 at exactly 1 code line, alert at 2). demo/ui/alert/index.ts:1-9 states the purpose in writing: "B.W2 ... converted it to a re-export ... The two consumers (ColorNutritionLabel.vue, Markdown.vue) import from this barrel unchanged." Dual path measured by this seat: `grep -rn 'from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"' demo/ | grep -v '^demo/ui/' | wc -l` → 18 direct; `grep -rnE 'from "(\.\./)+ui/[a-z-]+"' demo/ | wc -l` → 90 via the shim; and 8 files hold BOTH spellings at once (GradientVisualizer.vue, MixPane.vue, GenerateControls.vue, ConfigSliderPane.vue, ColorPicker.vue, ColorInput.vue, PaletteSlugBar.vue, PaletteCard.vue). glass-ui exposes no ./alert or ./skeleton subpath (checked against its exports map), so the shim buys not even tree-shaking granularity.
defects.mechanism: A layer whose stated reason to exist is that call sites should not have to change is a migration shim — edict 2 forbids exactly that, and edict 4 says the honest specifier is @mkbabb/glass-ui. Two names for one concept, with 8 files demonstrating the ambiguity is live rather than theoretical.
defects.reproduction: The census and the three greps above, fully reproduced by this seat in Revision 3 (the 90/18/8 dual-path measurement is new to this revision).
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ entirely and rewrite the ~92 call sites to the bare @mkbabb/glass-ui specifier. Purely mechanical, and L-1's re-keyed lattice is what keeps it from growing back. Cross-cutting rider, not this component's wave.

defects.defect: One public surface is described twice — once generated, once hand-copied — and the hand-copied description (tsconfig.demo.json#paths) is factually false about the surface it claims to enumerate.
defects.evidence: package.json#exports has exactly 7 keys and NO "." root key: ./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize (verified by this seat). tsconfig.demo.json#paths declares 8, of which 3 are phantoms naming absent files (@mkbabb/value.js -> dist/index.d.ts MISSING; /parsing -> MISSING; /units -> MISSING) and 2 real keys are undeclared (./css — 10 demo import sites, including useMarkdownColors.ts:4 — and ./value). 7 real, 8 declared, intersection 5.
defects.mechanism: vite.config.ts:41-50 GENERATES the runtime alias set from package.json#exports precisely so "the alias set can never drift from the exports map" — and the sibling mirror that must agree with it is hand-rolled and has drifted. Single-sourcing was applied to one of two mirrors; that asymmetry is the bug. Blast radius is nil today because exports self-resolution catches the misses, which is why this is MAJOR and not the BLOCKER a prior revision filed it as.
defects.reproduction: The exports enumeration is reproduced by this seat; the file-existence table and the tsc --traceResolution runs are Revision 2's, carried forward. Note Revision 3 endorses Revision 2's refutation of the earlier 'demo typechecks against the published tarball' BLOCKER as a probe artifact.
defects.proposedCure: Do not generate the paths map — DELETE it. Remove all seven @mkbabb/value.js* entries from tsconfig.demo.json; package.json#exports already resolves every key correctly and exhaustively from inside the repo. Zero entries = zero drift surface = no generator to maintain. Retain the vue/@vue/* entries, which pin instance identity and are load-bearing. Rider.

defects.defect: currentDoc = ref() is safe only by an ESM invariant the code never states, and the declared DocModule type admits the unsafe case. This narrows Revision 2's "Vue 3.5 idioms (edict 7) correct" negative proof, which is right about the call site and wrong about the contract.
defects.evidence: The negative half, measured (docs/.../Markdown/probe-L16-namespace.mjs): dynamic-import namespace isExtensible: false / ref(ns).value isReactive: false, isProxy: false / ref(ns).value === ns: true — Vue's getTargetType returns INVALID and reactive() bails. The positive half: markdown/index.ts:3 declares `export type DocModule = () => Promise<{ default: any }>` — nothing in that signature requires a module namespace, and Markdown.vue:45 accepts it as a PUBLIC prop. Driving the verbatim Markdown.vue:55/60/64-67 chain (ref(null) -> await module() -> computed(() => .default) -> h(...)) with `() => Promise.resolve({ default: Comp })`, via renderToString: "warn count: 1 / [Vue warn]: Vue received a Component that was made a reactive object. This can lead to unnecessary performance overhead and should be avoided by marking the component with markRaw or using shallowRef instead of ref." The same probe's control isolates the cause: ref(plainObj).value.default isReactive: true vs isReactive: false for the namespace.
defects.mechanism: The correctness of Markdown.vue:55 is not a property of Markdown.vue. It is a property of AboutPane.vue:82-92 choosing to pass () => import(...), plus an ESM spec guarantee (isExtensible === false on namespace objects) that appears nowhere in the type, the prop, or a comment. An invariant that lives only in the caller and only by accident is exactly what standing edict 7 asks to be made structural. This also gives L-10 (DocModule's `any`) the concrete cost it lacked: the `any` is the hole the reactive-component case comes through.
defects.reproduction: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/Markdown/probe-L16-shallowref.mjs — re-runs from its durable home and emits the warning verbatim. Filed MINOR deliberately, not inflated: no live call site triggers it, so it is a latent contract hole rather than a current misrender.
defects.proposedCure: shallowRef at Markdown.vue:55 — one word, and the whole declared type domain becomes safe instead of one call site. Under the greenfield lattice the type becomes Record<DisplayColorSpace, () => Promise<Component>> and the `any` dies with it, at which point shallowRef is correct by construction rather than by caller discipline. Lands inside wave MD-d; closing evidence probe-L16-shallowref.mjs emits `warn count: 0`.

defects.defect: onUpdated drives imperative TreeWalker + replaceChild mutation of DOM that a different Vue component owns, and the concept belongs at compile time in the markdown pipeline rather than at runtime.
defects.evidence: Markdown.vue:73-75 `onUpdated(() => { applyHighlighting(); })`; useMarkdownHighlighting.ts:24-65 walks the compiled .md component's text nodes and calls textNode.parentNode?.replaceChild(frag, textNode) on nodes Vue rendered. The correct home is available in place and empty: unplugin-vue-markdown exposes markdownItSetup / markdownItUses (types-CAs0WWKP.d.mts:150,154) and vite.config.ts:162 passes {}. Also note useMarkdownHighlighting is a "composable" with zero reactive state or lifecycle — a pure function wearing a use* name in a composables/ dir (edict 3, contrivance).
defects.mechanism: Ownership inversion across the VDOM boundary: a parent reaches into a child's rendered subtree and rewrites it, with only an idempotence guard (`if (body.querySelector("mark.cs-name")) return;` at :15) standing between it and repeated mutation. onUpdated is a shotgun — any parent-driven update re-runs the full scan.
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a hypothesis as to symptom. The imperative mutation and the onUpdated trigger are proven by file:line; I did not reproduce a patch conflict or a lost update.
defects.proposedCure: Replace TreeWalker + replaceChild with CSS.highlights + Range, which marks without mutating, and replace onUpdated with a post-flush watch on the space prop. useMarkdownHighlighting.ts (93 lines) collapses into a ~25-line markSpaceName.ts that receives the container from useTemplateRef instead of re-finding it by string (which also closes L-17's fourth dependent). The CSS.highlights transposition wants an owner ruling on the Safari support floor, so it is a rider rather than part of MD-d.

defects.defect: The component's `module` prop is mount-only: loadDocs runs solely from onMounted with no watch, so the component is correct only because its single consumer forces a remount with :key.
defects.evidence: Markdown.vue:58-62 loadDocs, :69-71 `onMounted(async () => { await loadDocs(); })` — no watch on `module` anywhere in the file. AboutPane.vue:52 supplies `:key="model.selectedColorSpace"`. `grep -rn 'Markdown' demo/` confirms exactly one consumer.
defects.mechanism: A public prop whose reactivity is delegated to the caller. A real consumer writing <Markdown :module="x" /> with a changing x silently renders stale content — the component's declared contract is wider than its implementation, and the compensating :key at the call site is a masking workaround (edict 2).
defects.reproduction: NONE for the stale render — proved by code structure (absence of any watch) rather than by a staged prop change, since this seat may not edit source to remove the :key.
defects.proposedCure: Add the internal `watch(() => module, loadDocs)` so the component honours its own prop, making the consumer's :key redundant rather than load-bearing. Wave MD-d.

defects.defect: The markdown/ barrel ships a dead export and an `any`, and is imported by the very component it exports.
defects.evidence: markdown/index.ts:5-9 `export interface DocItem { name; path; module }` — `grep -rn 'DocItem' demo/ src/ test/ e2e/` returns exactly one hit, its own declaration: zero consumers. :3 `export type DocModule = () => Promise<{ default: any }>` — the `any` is the hole L-16 exploits. Markdown.vue:40 imports DocModule from "./" — the barrel that re-exports Markdown.vue itself.
defects.mechanism: A barrel accumulating declarations nobody asked for, plus a circular module-graph edge (component -> its own barrel -> component) that exists only because the type had no better home.
defects.reproduction: The DocItem grep, reproduced by this seat.
defects.proposedCure: Delete markdown/index.ts entirely. DocItem goes with it; DocModule is replaced by the typed registry (L-5) at docs/registry.ts keyed Record<DisplayColorSpace, () => Promise<Component>>, which removes the `any` and the self-import together. Wave MD-d.

defects.defect: The ?source / @src / vite-source-export subsystem is fully dead, and this component's composable documents it as live load-bearing infrastructure.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure: module boundaries, ownership, direction of dependency, public surface
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, the tier declared at spawn. Declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — `resetDefaults()` (ConfigSliderPane.vue:92-94) is a shallow `Object.assign` over a nested config, so pressing Reset on /#/blob replaces `config.color` whole and destroys `color.paletteStops`, the live picker-derived ramp that BlobPane.vue:8-9 explicitly documents as NOT a slider. Reproduced with pasted node output: the user's 4-stop palette becomes glass-ui's canned 3-stop `["#b5947f","#d4b27d","#dad6b1"]`, and the recovery watch (useAtmosphere.ts:386-392) is keyed on colour change, so it never self-heals. Mechanism: reset semantics were re-minted demo-side and the re-mint is shape-blind — it never consults `sections`, the only description of what is a knob. glass-ui owns this concept (`useConfiguratorState.resetCurrent` + preset baselines + an injectable `clone` hook). The highest-leverage defect is the companion BLOCKER L-2: `variant="spectrum"` on 31 numeric sliders is the wrong public surface and one prop produces three independently measured defects (transparent value fill, a token-role-violating track re-ink, and 31 of the app's 39 worst-route tap-target failures at 12px wide).
result.negativeProof: Not SOUND, but four claims were refuted by measurement and recorded in §4 so they are not carried forward. (1) MY OWN hypothesis, refuted before publication: I measured that `tsconfig.demo.json`'s `paths` table misses `/css` and `/value`, that a frozen self-copy of value.js@4.0.0 sits in `node_modules` (materialised by keyframes.js's exact pin), and that the two copies differ by 34 lines in `css.d.ts` — and an out-of-package tsc probe appeared to show the demo typechecking the stale copy. Rerun with the probe file INSIDE the package (as every real demo/ file is), package self-reference wins and both subpaths resolve to the local `dist/`: type resolution and runtime resolution AGREE. Claim withdrawn; the `paths` block is dead weight (3 of 8 entries point at nonexistent files) but harmless, filed INFO not MAJOR. Two lessons recorded: a `Package ID` stamp in --traceResolution is not evidence of a node_modules read, and a probe placed outside the package under test measures a different program. (2)(3)(4) Three r2-report claims refuted: `.console-well` is NOT sound (glass-ui@7.0.0 ships `.glass-well`, satisfying the class's own declared retirement precondition); glass-ui does NOT need to be asked for a coarse hit-area extension (it ships two, `@utility touch-hit-area` and `[data-control-target]`, both curing BOTH axes where the demo's re-mint cures one); and the Copy-JSON action DOES have a shipped home (`DockControl`, already used for the identical copy action at GradientVisualizer.vue:254). Verified sound: dot-path traversal has exactly one home in the repo; the aurora Reset is safe because DEFAULT_AURORA_ATOMS omits `seed`; all 34 slider keys are live; `verbatimModuleSyntax` is honoured; Vue 3.5 idioms are correct; `--slider-track-bg` is a public producer token overridden on the container not per instance; no animation was deleted; the root-barrel import has no byte cost (r2's esbuild measurement adopted); and the coarse hit-area IS reached on tablets (I hypothesised dead code and measured it live-but-redundant).

defects.defect: `resetDefaults()` is a shallow `Object.assign(config, structuredClone(defaults))` over a nested config graph, so Reset overwrites whole atom subtrees including derived state that is not a slider — destroying the live picker→blob palette coupling.
defects.evidence: demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:92-94; invariant stated and broken at demo/scenes/blob/BlobPane.vue:8-9; writer at demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphere.ts:386-393. Pasted: `node --input-type=module -e "import { BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS } from '@mkbabb/glass-ui/blob-config'; const live = structuredClone(BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS); live.color.paletteStops = ['#112233','#445566','#778899','#aabbcc']; Object.assign(live, structuredClone(BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS)); console.log(live.color.paletteStops)"` → `after resetDefaults(), paletteStops = ["#b5947f","#d4b27d","#dad6b1"]` (4 stops → 3, user colour gone).
defects.mechanism: Reset semantics re-minted demo-side; the re-mint is shape-blind because the only description of what is a knob (the `sections` table) is never consulted. glass-ui owns the concept: `useConfiguratorState.resetCurrent()` restores a declared preset baseline with an injectable `clone` hook (useConfiguratorState.d.ts:9-14,42).
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/blob at ≥1024px, change the picker colour so the blob repaints, then press Reset in the pane footer. The blob reverts to the canned tan ramp and stays wrong until the picker colour next changes. The node one-liner above reproduces it headlessly against the installed glass-ui@7.0.0.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `resetDefaults`. Adopt `useConfiguratorState<BlobConfig>({ presets: BLOB_PRESETS })` and wire `@reset="resetCurrent"`; derived state (paletteStops) then lives outside the preset table by construction. Do NOT patch by iterating `sections` — that keeps a second home for reset alive.

defects.defect: `variant="spectrum"` is the wrong design-system variant for 31 abstract numeric sliders. One prop produces three independently measured defects: no value fill, a token-role-violating track re-ink, and 31 sub-24px tap targets.
defects.evidence: demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:146. glass-ui contract in dist/glass-ui.css: `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-range{background:0 0}` and `.slider-thumb{width:calc(var(--slider-thumb-size,1rem)*.75)}`. Measured WebKit 1440 on /#/blob: `{rowCount:31, trackBackground:"oklch(0.446872 0.003862 34.629978)", trackBackgroundImage:"none", rangeBackground:"rgba(0,0,0,0)", rangeWidth:"163.46875px"}`. Audit: REPORT.md:41 — /#/blob = 39 smallTapTargets, worst of all 60 captures (next worst 8); REPORT.json lists 31 entries of `{"w":12,"h":24,"tag":"span","label":"Body Radius"|"Satellites"|…}`; threshold is WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 at capture.mjs:98 (`m.w < 24 || m.h < 24`). Still RED on touch: measured 12×44 at 390 coarse. Visual: shots/safari-desktop-light/blob.png shows 31 charcoal slabs beside the picker's four real spectra.
defects.mechanism: A design-system variant whose contract is 'the consumer paints a gradient; there is no filled/unfilled split; the thumb is a narrow position marker' was applied to a population that has no spectrum. The author then treated the resulting invisibility as a fact to work around (ConfigSliderPane.vue:190-202 documents the whole detour) rather than as evidence of the wrong primitive, and fed the text-ink token `--ink-muted` into the control-surface variable `--slider-track-bg`.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/blob at 1440. `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.config-console .slider-range')).backgroundColor` → `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` with `width` 163px; `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.config-console .slider-track')).backgroundImage` → `none`. Thumb `getBoundingClientRect()` → 12×24.
defects.proposedCure: `variant="standard"`, and delete `--slider-track-bg` (:202) and the `:deep(.configurator-row .font-mono)` re-ink (:204-206) with it. Three defects, one root, one prop.

defects.defect: glass-ui `./configurator` ships five primitives written for these two panes by name; the demo consumes one (`ConfiguratorRow`) and re-rolls four. A sixth, `InstrumentChassis`, has zero demo consumers.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/configurator/index.d.ts exports Configurator, ConfiguratorLayer, ConfiguratorRow, CONFIGURATOR_SIZE_KEY/ConfiguratorSize, useConfiguratorState. ConfiguratorLayer.vue.d.ts:5-7 names the consumer: "blob has Mood / Body / Surface / Color / Motion / Pointer / Render". ConfiguratorRow.vue.d.ts:19 annotates its double-label API "(value.js L14)". Demo re-mints: section group at ConfigSliderPane.vue:232-243, footer at :245-251, density clamp at :215-217, reset at :92-94. `grep -rn "InstrumentChassis" demo/ | wc -l` → 0, while the primitive ships `stage`/`inspector`/`action` slots with `boundaries: "inspector-action"`.
defects.mechanism: Producer-consumer inversion: the design system built the exact surface on this repo's own request (L14), and the consumer adopted 1 of 9 available pieces and rebuilt the rest inside a feature area. The component's own header comment (:6-10) calls the re-mints "thin structural shells, not the row primitive" — factually wrong for two of them.
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a static-surface comparison, fully evidenced by the pasted `index.d.ts` and the demo grep counts.
defects.proposedCure: Transpose to `<Configurator scroll-mode="auto" size="sm">` + `<ConfiguratorLayer>` per section + `<ConfiguratorRow>` + `useConfiguratorState`. The component's entire 74-line `<style>` block goes to zero and `ConfigSliderPane.vue` is deleted in favour of two ~25-line studio SFCs (full source in report §5).

defects.defect: The published library declares a 5.2 MB Vue design system and a package with zero importers as runtime `dependencies`; direction of dependency inverted and the package graph is cyclic.
defects.evidence: package.json:99-102 `"dependencies": { "@mkbabb/glass-ui": "^7.0.0", "@mkbabb/keyframes.js": "^6.0.0" }`. `npm ls @mkbabb/value.js` → `@mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 ├─┬ @mkbabb/glass-ui@7.0.0 │ └── @mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 └─┬ @mkbabb/keyframes.js@6.0.0 └── @mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 deduped`. `grep -rl "@mkbabb/glass-ui" src/ | wc -l` → 0; `grep -rl "@mkbabb/keyframes" src/ demo/ | wc -l` → 0; `grep -rl "@mkbabb/glass-ui" demo/ | wc -l` → 82. `du -sh` → glass-ui 5.2M, keyframes.js 608K, self-copy 168K. tsconfig.demo.json:26-27 states the contradicted invariant: "the library program never [sees glass-ui] (inv-K-1 — structurally glass-ui-free)".
defects.mechanism: The demo's dependencies were declared on the library's manifest. keyframes.js hard-pins `"@mkbabb/value.js": "4.0.0"`, so npm materialises a frozen tarball of this package inside its own node_modules — already 34 lines diverged from the local build in css.d.ts. glass-ui is blameless: it declares value.js as an OPTIONAL peerDependency, the correct shape.
defects.reproduction: `npm ls @mkbabb/value.js` prints the cycle. `npm i @mkbabb/value.js` in a clean project pulls 5.8 MB plus a Vue 3 + reka-ui + Tailwind v4 peer graph for a CSS-value library.
defects.proposedCure: `@mkbabb/glass-ui` → devDependencies (it is the demo's; 82 demo files, 0 src files). `@mkbabb/keyframes.js` → deleted (0 importers repo-wide). The published dependency graph becomes empty, the cycle dissolves, the self-copy stops existing, and the tsconfig.demo.json `paths` block can then be deleted safely (verified in report §4.1).

defects.defect: `demo/ui/` is a 19-directory pure-alias shim over the glass-ui root barrel, load-bearing for 50 files / 90 imports, codified by a DESIGN.md rule that cites two paths which no longer exist. This component imports the same package through three different dialects in one eight-line block.
defects.evidence: `find demo/ui -type f | wc -l` → 19; `find demo/ui -name "*.vue" | wc -l` → 0. `cat demo/ui/card/index.ts` → `export { Card, CardHeader, … } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`. `grep -rho 'from "[^"]*ui/[a-z-]*"' demo/ | grep -v glass-ui | wc -l` → 90 across 50 files. glass-ui ships ./button, ./card, ./slider, ./select as first-class subpaths. demo/DESIGN.md:384 mandates `@components/ui/alert` — an alias killed at W43/RF-15 (tsconfig.demo.json:32-35); DESIGN.md:304 describes `demo/@/components/ui/` as holding shadcn-vue components, a directory with 0 .vue files. ConfigSliderPane.vue:16-23 mixes the shim (16-18), subpaths (20-21) and the root barrel (23).
defects.mechanism: An ergonomics-only indirection layer survived the migration that emptied it of implementations, and the governing doc rule froze it in place while its own citations rotted. Owner edict 2: no aliases, no dual paths.
defects.reproduction: NONE — static, fully enumerated by the pasted greps.
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/; rewrite the 90 imports to `@mkbabb/glass-ui/<subpath>`; delete DESIGN.md:384 and correct :304. For this component that collapses three dialects to one and moves `writeClipboard` onto its own door (`@mkbabb/glass-ui/dom`).

defects.defect: The rule literally named "THE ONE RHYTHM SOURCE" exists as two byte-identical copies in two files, and the copies produce two different rhythms — 36px vs 61px. On this population the clamp is inert dead CSS.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "clamp(2rem, 7cqi, 2.625rem)" demo/` → demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:216 and demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:332. Prose duplicated at ConfigSliderPane.vue:208-210 and ComponentSliders.vue:325-326. Measured WebKit 1440 on the same page: `{channelStripHeight:36, channelStripMinBlock:"35.84px", configuratorRowHeight:61, configuratorRowMinBlock:"35.84px"}` — the picker binds, the config row's intrinsic 61px never touches the 35.84px floor. 61/36 = 1.69×, the same order as the 1.83× discontinuity ComponentSliders.vue:319-322 says the law retired. Container check: `.config-console` containerType `normal`, nearest size container `.pane-wrapper` at 512px (demo/styles/shell.css:82-84), so 7cqi = 35.84px.
defects.mechanism: A cross-population invariant was expressed by copying a CSS declaration instead of by adopting the producer's density axis, so nothing enforces that the copies agree — and they do not.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/blob at 1440; `document.querySelector('.channel-strip').getBoundingClientRect().height` → 36; `document.querySelector('.config-console .configurator-row').getBoundingClientRect().height` → 61.
defects.proposedCure: Delete both copies. `ConfiguratorSize` (size.d.ts:1-20) cascades via provide/inject; set `size` once on `<Configurator>`. If the picker's exact clamp is wanted it becomes a glass-ui relay (report §6.3), never a demo class.

defects.defect: The coarse-pointer hit-area extension re-mints a utility glass-ui already ships, cures the axis that was already passing, and is a measured no-op on its own axis.
defects.evidence: demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:218-230 sets `block-size: max(100%, var(--dock-touch-target, 2.75rem))` on a `::before`. glass-ui ships `@utility touch-hit-area` (dist/styles/utilities/a11y-overrides.css) with BOTH `min-width` and `min-height`, and `[data-control-target]` (dist/styles/utilities/responsive.css) with both `min-block-size` and `min-inline-size`. Measured at 1024 with hasTouch: `{pointerCoarse:true, sliderHostHeight:44, pseudoBlockSize:"44px"}` — glass-ui's own coarse density clamp (dist/styles/tokens/light-dark.css `--control-floor: var(--touch-target)`) already brings `.glass-slider` from 24px (fine) to 44px (coarse), so `max(44px, 44px)` is a no-op. The failing axis is width: thumb measured 12×24 at 1440 and 12×44 at 390 coarse — a pseudo on the parent cannot change the focusable element's box.
defects.mechanism: A producer-owned a11y concern was re-solved consumer-side, at half the scope, against the producer's internal class names, for a defect whose real axis the re-mint does not touch. It also borrows the dock's `--dock-touch-target` where the general `--touch-target` is the right token (both 2.75rem today, so scope-borrow not breakage).
defects.reproduction: Launch WebKit at 1024×768 with hasTouch, goto /#/blob: `matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)').matches` → true, `.glass-slider` height 44 both with and without the demo rule; `.slider-thumb` width stays 12.
defects.proposedCure: Delete :218-230. Fix the width at its root by dropping `variant="spectrum"` (L-2); if a hit extension is still wanted, apply the producer's `touch-hit-area` utility or `[data-control-target]`.

defects.defect: A raw `<Button variant="ghost" size="sm">` is placed inside `<GlassDock>` where glass-ui ships `DockControl` and where the demo already uses `DockControl` for the identical copy-to-clipboard action.
defects.evidence: demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:164-173. DockControl.vue.d.ts:12-16 guarantees "the HIT CELL stays the full --dock-control-size (≥44px on coarse via the density clamp) — hit box ≠ paint box". Demo idiom in 4 files: GradientVisualizer.vue:13,254 (`<DockControl compact title="Copy CSS" @click="copyCSS">` — the same action), MixResultDisplay.vue:3, ExtractWorkbench.vue:187, ExtractControls.vue:98. Measured WebKit 1440: `actionBarButtons: [{label:"Copy JSON", w:135, h:36}, {label:"Reset", w:89, h:36}]`.
defects.mechanism: Dual path for 'a control inside a dock'. The bypassed primitive is the one carrying the coarse hit-cell guarantee, so the shortcut costs exactly the property the primitive exists to provide.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/blob at 1440; `[...document.querySelectorAll('.config-action-bar button')].map(b=>b.getBoundingClientRect().height)` → [36, 36].
defects.proposedCure: `<DockControl>`; better, delete the bespoke dock entirely and use `Configurator`'s `footer` slot, which already receives `{ reset }`.

defects.defect: `.pane-scroll-fade` fades nothing, is applied here against its own documented contract, and hand-rolls a vertical scroll port that glass-ui ships and the demo has already adopted once.
defects.evidence: Sole definition at demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:54-57 sets only `contain` and `scroll-timeline`. Measured WebKit 1440: `{scrollFadeMask:"none", scrollFadeContain:"content", scrollFadeScrollTimeline:"--pane-scroll", scrollHeights:{client:695, scroll:2605}}`; at 390 `{client:636, scroll:3071}` (4.8× overflow, no affordance). PaneHeader.vue:43-46 states the class "lives on the ROOT element of each pane Card (… ConfigSlider)"; ConfigSliderPane.vue:106 puts it on an inner div while 8 sibling panes put it on the Card root (GradientPane.vue:20, MixPane.vue:62, ExtractPane.vue:5, GeneratePane.vue:31, AboutPane.vue:4, BrowsePane.vue:2, AdminPane.vue:2, PalettesPane.vue:2). glass-ui ships `FadingScroll` (axis x|y, fadeStart, fadeEnd, ariaLabel) and `Configurator scrollMode`; the demo already uses it at EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:84 with axis="x".
defects.mechanism: A behaviour was removed but its name kept, producing a class that promises a fade across 9 consumers and delivers none — while the design system's real fading scroll port sits installed and proven in-repo for the horizontal case only.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/blob at 1440; `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.pane-scroll-fade')).maskImage` → `"none"`, `clientHeight/scrollHeight` → 695/2605.
defects.proposedCure: `Configurator scroll-mode="auto"` (or `<FadingScroll axis="y">`) and delete `.pane-scroll-fade` from this component. Repo-wide, rename the class to what it does or replace it with `FadingScroll` at all nine sites — a separate wave.

defects.defect: `/#/blob` renders 0 of 31 rows below `lg`: the URL resolves the pane but the mobile single-pane segment ignores the route and stays on Picker. Deep links to this scene are broken on half the matrix.
defects.evidence: Measured WebKit 390×844 isMobile, goto /#/blob: `{hash:"#/blob?space=lab&color=…", configConsolePresent:false, rowCount:0, actionBarPresent:false, paneHeaderTitles:[], bodyTextLen:69}`. Audit corroboration: REPORT.md:157 records /#/blob at 69 chars mobile vs 713 desktop — the largest desktop/mobile text delta of any route. shots/safari-mobile-light/blob.png shows the segmented control reading "Picker | Blob" with Picker selected. After clicking the "Blob" segment: `{configConsolePresent:true, rowCount:31, sliderH:44, thumb:{w:12,h:44}, scroll:{client:636, scroll:3071}}`.
defects.mechanism: Two tables that can disagree — the route table (demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:78,92) and the mobile content-pane segment default — and they do. A scene has no say in its own addressability. No layout gate is involved: the pane renders fully once the segment is clicked.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/blob in a 390px-wide WebKit context. The colour picker renders; the pane title and all 31 rows are absent from the DOM. Click the "Blob" segment and all 31 appear.
defects.proposedCure: Generate the router FROM a single `views.ts` table (`ViewId → { component, mobileSegment, label, icon }`) so a route cannot exist without a segment. Shell-owned, but carried with this component because it is why its entire surface is URL-unreachable on mobile.

defects.defect: `.console-well` is an interim demo class whose own documented retirement precondition — the producer's `.glass-well` rung — is already satisfied at the installed glass-ui@7.0.0.
defects.evidence: demo/styles/foundation.css:339-354: "INTERIM demo class — swaps onto the producer `.glass-well` rung when packet P3 ships (BOOKED, T.W3 §BOOKS)." Producer rung present: `grep -o "\.glass-well[^{]*{[^}]*}" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/glass/surface-axis.css` → `.glass-well { --glass-well-tone: 8%; background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--card), var(--foreground) var(--glass-well-tone)); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 2px …; border-radius: var(--radius-md); }`. glass-ui also ships a `Surface` component with a tier/material/deep axis. Measured: `.config-console` and `.console-well` are the same element (ConfigSliderPane.vue:122), so one box is styled from two files.
defects.mechanism: A self-declared interim duplicate outlived its sunset condition; nothing watches for the condition being met, so the second home persists silently.
defects.reproduction: NONE — static; the pasted producer CSS and the demo comment are the whole proof.
defects.proposedCure: Execute the booked swap: replace `.console-well` with the producer `.glass-well` rung (or `<Surface>`), delete the demo class from foundation.css. This also refutes the r2 report's classification of `.console-well` as sound.

defects.defect: Two `:deep()` reaches across the package boundary into glass-ui-internal class names, plus a per-instance Tailwind override where the producer ships a declarative density axis.
defects.evidence: demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:204-206 (`:deep(.configurator-row .font-mono)`), :215-217 (`:deep(.configurator-row)`), :219-229 (`:deep(.configurator-row .glass-slider)`), and :143 `class="gap-1.5 py-1"`. ConfiguratorRow.vue.d.ts:22-28 names the anti-pattern: "All three are declarative props, so a consumer expresses a double-label row WITHOUT a `:deep()` reach into the slot or a hand-rolled in-slot sans+mono pair." ConfiguratorRow ships `size?: ConfiguratorSize` with a documented prop→inject→baked resolution order.
defects.mechanism: Producer class names are not a public API; a rename in glass-ui breaks these rules with no typecheck, no lint and no test. The pane adopted the row's `name` prop and then reached past it anyway to re-ink the result. Owner edict 5 forbids per-instance overrides.
defects.reproduction: NONE — static; the selectors and the producer docblock are the evidence.
defects.proposedCure: `size="sm"` on the row (or once on `<Configurator>`); the readout ink becomes a glass-ui relay ask for a `--configurator-row-name-ink` token rather than a `:deep()`.

defects.defect: `writeClipboard`'s failure-explicit discriminated result is discarded, in a package that advertises failure-explicitness and whose own demo ships the correct feedback idiom in two other files.
defects.evidence: demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:88-90 `await writeClipboard(JSON.stringify(config, null, 2));` — no `ok` check, no confirmation. Producer: dist/composables/dom/useClipboard.d.ts:31-37 "Returns the discriminated result (`{ ok }` / `{ ok, reason }`) rather than a lossy boolean… `const { ok } = await writeClipboard(text)`"; `CopyFailureReason = "clipboard-api" | "no-api"`. Correct idiom already in-repo: demo/workbenches/mix/MixResultDisplay.vue:31 and demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientEasingEditor.vue:94 both use `useClipboard({ resetMs })` and bind `status`. package.json:4 advertises "failure-explicit".
defects.mechanism: Third path: 'copy with feedback' already has two homes in the demo (`useClipboard` with status) and this pane chose neither, so a clipboard failure is indistinguishable from success.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the failure branch without a permissions-denied context; the discarded return value is static at :89 and the absent feedback is visible in shots/safari-desktop-light/blob.png (no confirmation affordance on the Copy JSON control).
defects.proposedCure: `const { status, copy } = useClipboard({ resetMs: 1500 })` and bind `status` to the control, matching MixResultDisplay; or move the action into `Configurator`'s footer slot.

defects.defect: The pane's contract types are exported from a `.vue` file, generic object-graph plumbing is trapped inside `<script setup>`, and `config: Record<string, unknown>` erases both consumers' types — forcing four `as unknown as` casts and a 12-line hand-rolled mapped type to plug the hole.
defects.evidence: demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:27-39 exports `SliderDef`/`SliderSection` from an SFC; imported back at AuroraPane.vue:34 and BlobPane.vue:15. `readPath`/`writePath` at :57-73 are Vue-free and unreachable/untestable. Props typed `Record<string, unknown>` at :41-52, forcing BlobPane.vue:124,126 and AuroraPane.vue:111,113 to double-cast. BlobPane.vue:36-48 pays for the hole with a homomorphic mapped type `NumericAtomPath` needing `-?` at two levels; AuroraPane has no guard at all.
defects.mechanism: The schema of the pane protocol is data, not view, and was housed in a view file; the erased prop type then pushed the type safety back onto one consumer, unevenly.
defects.reproduction: NONE — static; the four casts and the mapped type are visible at the cited lines.
defects.proposedCure: Make the component generic: `SliderDef<T>` with `key: NumericPath<T>`, in a `.ts` module (`demo/studios/config-path.ts`), with `NumericPath<T>` promoted from BlobPane and `read`/`write` exported as plain functions. The double casts and the per-consumer guard both disappear. Ideally relay `NumericPath<T>` to glass-ui so all `Configurator` consumers share it.

defects.defect: An object-spread ternary is used to forward one optional string prop, a contrivance created by `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` against dead optionality.
defects.evidence: demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:107 `<PaneHeader v-bind="description !== undefined ? { description } : {}">`; tsconfig.base.json:12 `"exactOptionalPropertyTypes": true`; PaneHeader.vue props `description?: string`. Both consumers always pass one: AuroraPane.vue:115, BlobPane.vue:128.
defects.mechanism: A compiler constraint was worked around at the call site instead of fixed at the contract, and the optionality it works around is never exercised.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) of `demo/scenes/about/markdown/Markdown.vue`
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model ID `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M context). Seat was spawned with an explicit Opus 5 declaration; the declaration is present and matches what I observe myself to be. No inherited or undeclared seat.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the component's headline design idea (a per-color certified accent ink giving the About document a chromatic heading voice) does not exist in dark mode. Measured OKLab ΔE between rungs collapses 8.3× from light to dark: h2-vs-prose 0.3153 → 0.0378, h3-vs-prose 0.1938 → 0.0230, h2-vs-h3 0.1215 → 0.0149 — every dark value at or below the ~0.02 small-text JND. Accent chroma collapses 9.1× (C 0.1887 → 0.0208). The three-rung ink ladder is one perceptual ink in dark. This is not a solver bug: `certifyAccentInk` meets its stated WCAG-floor obligation. The design obligation is wrong — a contrast floor with no separation floor guarantees legibility and nothing else, so the scheme with the least chromatic headroom is the scheme where the idea silently disappears. Light and dark are two different designs wearing one name.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the verdict (DEFECTIVE), but recorded so the challenge is honest about what it could not break: (1) MOTION IS SOUND — the `transition: color var(--duration-slow)` on headings (Markdown.vue:125) and `transition-colors duration-fast` on links (:201,:405) are all neutralised by the global guard at demo/styles/animations.css:184-193 (`transition-duration: 0.01ms !important` on `*`); no transitioned property forces layout (only `color`/`text-decoration`); no keyframes were deleted (edict 6 clean). (2) NO HORIZONTAL OVERFLOW AT ANY ARM — measured docHorizontalOverflow 0, cardHorizontalOverflow 0 at 390px; katexOverflowing 0 at both 1440 and 390; the AB-1 `:has(> .katex-display)` overflow repair genuinely works and REPORT.md records horizontalOverflow 0 across all 60 captures. (3) INLINE-CODE CONTRAST PASSES — certified accent on the well measures 5.82:1 (above the 4.5:1 floor for the 12px run) and the h2 accent on the plate 6.58:1; the certifyAccentInk path does real work in light. (4) THE AB-3 WELL CURE HOLDS IN THE POPULATED STATE — codeBg oklab(0.913299…) light / oklab(0.345296…) dark, stepping the same direction as the plate in both schemes. (5) NO CONSOLE OR PAGE ERRORS attributable to this component; the only /#/ console error is the dev VITE_API_URL warning. (6) SCRIPT-SIDE EDICTS CLEAN — verbatimModuleSyntax correct (`import type` at Markdown.vue:40 and useMarkdownHighlighting.ts:1), Vue 3.5 idioms correct (useTemplateRef :50, reactive props destructure :44-48), no legacy shims, no dual paths, no invented demo/ui wrapper. The contrivance is entirely in the 331-line stylesheet, not the 76 script lines.

defects.defect: The certified-accent heading ink system collapses to a single perceptual ink in dark mode: every rung of the h2/h3/prose ladder falls at or below the OKLab JND, an 8.3x weakening from light. The component's headline design idea does not exist in the dark scheme.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/Markdown/evidence/M2-rhythm-inks-light.json and M3-rhythm-inks-dark.json. Measured deltaE_ok — h2 vs prose: LIGHT 0.3153 / DARK 0.0378 (8.3x); h3 vs prose: 0.1938 / 0.0230 (8.4x); mark vs prose: 0.3153 / 0.0378; h2 vs h3: 0.1215 / 0.0149 (8.2x). Accent chroma: light C=0.1887 -> dark C=0.0208 (9.1x collapse); dark accent = oklch(95.83% 0.021 9.83). Consuming sites: Markdown.vue:163,172,187,252,312; producer useMarkdownColors.ts:55-79. Visual: evidence/E2-populated-desktop-dark.png shows h2, h3 and prose all as plain white.
defects.mechanism: certifyAccentInk enforces a WCAG contrast FLOOR against the plate but carries no SEPARATION obligation from the body ink or the adjacent rung. Against a dark plate the floor walk has nowhere to go but toward white, so lightness rises to 0.958 and chroma is gamut-mapped to 0.021. The h3 rung then mixes 61.8% of an already-near-white accent toward an already-near-white foreground, producing zero step.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/Markdown/evidence/probe4.mjs light ; node .../probe4.mjs dark ; compare the deltaEok blocks. Dev server must be live at http://localhost:9000.
defects.proposedCure: Make the ink contract two-sided in the producer: certifyAccentInk gains a minSeparation obligation alongside its floor. When the floor walk would cross the separation minimum, the rung changes CARRIER (weight, size, or a rule) rather than silently converging on the body ink. Acceptance bench already exists: h2-vs-prose deltaE_ok >= 0.10 and h2-vs-h3 >= 0.05 in BOTH schemes, measured by probe4.mjs.

defects.defect: The designed error state is structurally unreachable, and the real doc-load failure mode tears down the entire route — picker included — instead of degrading in place.
defects.evidence: Markdown.vue:58-62 — `currentDoc.value = await module(); isLoading.value = false;` with no try/catch, so a rejection leaves isLoading true forever and the v-else Alert branch (Markdown.vue:19-31, "Oh snap...") can never render. Rejection escapes onMounted (:69-71) into ErrorBoundary (demo/color-picker/App.vue:50-140, onErrorCaptured at ErrorBoundary.vue:59) which wraps the whole workspace. Measured with /assets/docs/*.md aborted: {"aboutCardPresent": false, "skeletonsPresent": 0, "markdownWrapperPresent": false, "alertPresent": false, "ohSnapPresent": false} — evidence/M7-failure-state.json. Screenshot evidence/E6-doc-load-failure-whole-route-collapse.png: both panes gone, bare "Try again" button on the ambient field. Also AboutPane.vue:50-51 already guards v-if="activeMarkdownModule", so the Alert's copy describes a condition the parent prevents — doubly dead. Violates PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:52 (PR-08) and VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83.
defects.mechanism: An async lifecycle hook with no failure ownership. The success path is the only path the state machine models; the failure path exits the function before the state transition, so the third rendered branch is dead template and the rejection becomes the parent's problem.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/Markdown/evidence/probe6.mjs failure — routes /assets/docs/*.md to abort('failed'), waits 9s, then reads the DOM and screenshots.
defects.proposedCure: The loader owns its failure. Three explicit states (loading | ready | failed) driven by try/catch/finally; the failed state renders IN PLACE as a named, retryable role="status" region scoped to the document region — not a stock Alert, and never an app-level unmount. Delete the unreachable Alert branch entirely (its copy is obsolete against the parent guard).

defects.defect: `content-visibility: auto` with `contain-intrinsic-size: auto 200px` on 33 of 34 direct children inflates the About card's scrollHeight by 63% on first paint; the scrollbar lies and shrinks as the reader scrolls.

The rule also leaks onto runtime-injected nodes — my first ch-measurement probe returned a bogus 231ch because the injected span inherited contain-intrinsic-size and reported width 200px.
defects.mechanism: A blanket `> *:not(:first-child)` selector applies a single fixed intrinsic-size guess to every element species in the document, including 1px horizontal rules and 32px headings, and to anything appended at runtime.

Markdown.vue uses text-base, leading-7, text-4xl/3xl/2xl/xl/lg, text-xs, text-sm (44 @apply across 57 selectors) and font-display on h1..h6 (:121). Corpus: 53 h2 + 85 h3 = 138 headings all rendering in the identity voice.
defects.mechanism: The stylesheet was authored against Tailwind's default scale rather than against the glass-ui role tokens, so every size utility silently carries the wrong family and the wrong rung — the exact root-cause class the file's own T.W4-6 comment (Markdown.vue:21-25) identifies and then re-commits for headings.

defects.defect: The declared golden-ratio ladder is not the rendered ladder — 20 of 33 adjacent-sibling intervals are collapsed margins, and PR-35 requires About's collapsed-margin count to be recorded as 0.
defects.evidence: OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:100 (PR-35): "No margin collapse..." and "record ... collapsed-margin count `0`". Representative rows: UL->H3 declares 16px + 25.875px = 41.88 sum, renders 25.88; P->HR declares 16px + 41.875px = 57.88, renders 41.88; HR->H2 declares 41.875px + 41.875px = 83.75, renders 41.88.
