defects.mechanism: Every interval is declared twice — as the preceding block's margin-bottom and the following block's margin-top — and normal-flow sibling margin collapse renders the max of the two. ` two-pane grid; ErrorBoundary.vue:59 `onErrorCaptured` returns false. Measured: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/Markdown/probe-C3.mjs abort` → {"aboutCardPresent": false, "mdBody": false, "wrapper": false, "skeletons": 0, "trap": {"rejections": [], "errors": []}, tailHTML ends `…lucide-rotate-ccw…> Try again
`}. Frame: frames/C3-abort.png shows the entire app replaced by a bare "Try again" button.
defects.mechanism: unguarded-async-rejection escalating through a coarse-grained error boundary; designed fallback branch has no reachable input state

defects.defect: ConfigSliderPane's public surface is stringly typed (`config: Record<string, unknown>`, `SliderDef.key: string`), so type safety cannot be enforced at the boundary and is instead re-derived per consumer — BlobPane wrote a 30-line mapped-type guard, AuroraPane has none.
defects.evidence: demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:27-40 declares `export interface SliderDef { key: string; … }` and props `config: Record<string, unknown>` / `defaults: Record<string, unknown>`. The complete set of laundering casts in the demo is exactly the four call sites of this component: AuroraPane.vue:111 `(atoms as unknown) as Record<string, unknown>`, AuroraPane.vue:113, BlobPane.vue:124, BlobPane.vue:126. BlobPane.vue:19-45 re-invents path validity in ~30 lines of mapped types with the comment "A typo or an abrogated key fails typecheck here rather than silently no-op'ing a slider". AuroraPane.vue:97-106 declares "colorEnergy", "noise", "zones.count" as bare strings with no equivalent guard.
defects.mechanism: `Record<string, unknown>` + `key: string` is the type-theoretic equivalent of no contract; a shared module that cannot express its own invariant pushes the invariant into every caller, and two callers produced two different answers.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "as unknown) as Record<string, unknown>" demo  -> exactly four lines, all four call sites of ConfigSliderPane. Read ConfigSliderPane.vue:28 — `key: string` admits every string.
defects.proposedCure: Make the pane a generic SFC (`<script setup lang="ts" generic="T extends object">`) with `SliderDef<T> { key: NumericPath<T>; … }` and `config: T; defaults: T`. Move BlobPane's NumericPath mapped type INTO the shared module where it is written once. All four `as unknown as` casts disappear, BlobPane's guard is hoisted rather than deleted, and AuroraPane gains the guard it never had. Vue 3.5 supports generic defineProps today — no contrivance.

defects.defect: The Select handlers are typed against reka-ui's `AcceptableValue` — glass-ui's internal substrate, a devDependency-only package — rather than glass-ui's own emitted `SelectionValue`. The declared domain is strictly wider than the emitter's codomain and the gap is bridged by an unconditional `String(v) as X` coercion.
defects.evidence: AuroraPane.vue:25 `import type { AcceptableValue } from "reka-ui";` — package.json lists reka-ui under devDependencies ("^2.9"); the only runtime dependencies are @mkbabb/glass-ui and @mkbabb/keyframes.js. glass-ui emits its own type: dist/components/select/Select.vue.d.ts `export interface SelectEmits { "update:modelValue": [value: SelectionValue]; … }` with dist/components/_shared/selection.d.ts `export type SelectionValue = string | number;`. reka-ui's is wider: dist/index3.d.ts:231 `type AcceptableValue = string | number | bigint | Record<string, any> | null;`. Four demo files do this (AuroraPane.vue:25, GradientVisualizer.vue:28, MixConfigBar.vue:15, GenerateControls.vue:33). `grep -l SelectionValue node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/*.d.ts` returns NOTHING — the correct type is unnameable by a consumer.
defects.mechanism: AuroraPane.vue:79 `atoms.harmony = String(v) as AuroraHarmony` is a masking fallback against cases glass-ui cannot emit (String(null)->"null", String({})->"[object Object]"), while the case that CAN occur (SelectionValue includes number) is silently accepted — String(3) as AuroraHarmony writes a garbage atom with no guard. Typing against the true string|number would force that branch into the open.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'from "reka-ui"' demo  -> four files; grep -l SelectionValue node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/*.d.ts -> no output.
defects.proposedCure: COORDINATION PACKET P-2 to glass-ui: re-export `SelectionValue` from @mkbabb/glass-ui/select (it is already the declared emit type but is not on the public surface). Then all four handlers type against it and narrow explicitly (`typeof v === "string"`) instead of coercing, and the reka-ui reach disappears.

defects.mechanism: two transports for one domain fact — prop-drilled whole-model v-model alongside the ambient pipeline injection — inside a single feature
defects.reproduction: NONE (structural; read the three files). The secondary perf claim (props identity churn per colour tick via usePaneRouter.ts:168-175) is labelled a HYPOTHESIS — the subtree legitimately re-inks per frame for componentInk, so the waste was not isolated.
defects.proposedCure: Replace defineModel with `inject(COLOR_MODEL_KEY)` and take zero props, as ConsoleRail already does. That deletes the `about` case in usePaneRouter and AboutPane's forwarding defineModel. Lands naturally with the ARCHITECTURE §1 requirement that About become the standalone `/about` route rather than Picker's permanent right-hand pane (viewSchema.ts:107 `right: "about"`).

defects.defect: The channel display-scale rule is copy-pasted five times across four files; two of the copies are the same function.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "max <= 1" demo/` → ColorNutritionLabel.vue:220, picker/display/ColorComponentDisplay/readoutReservation.ts:98, color-session/useColorParsing.ts:98, color-session/useSliderGradients.ts:73, color-session/useSliderGradients.ts:84 — all `meta.unit === "%" && meta.max <= 1 ? 100 : 1`. ColorNutritionLabel.vue:222-227 and useSliderGradients.ts:85 are behaviourally identical bound-formatters.
defects.mechanism: a property of ChannelMeta implemented at every call site instead of beside the type (picker-color.ts:40-46)
defects.reproduction: NONE (structural). Consequence visible on screen: the label prints OKLCh C as "0 to 0.5" (the raw physical max) without saying whether it means the raw or the CSS percentage reference, which ARCHITECTURE §2 fixes at 0.4.
defects.proposedCure: One exported `formatChannelBound` beside the ChannelSpec — in the library per L-3's cure, or at minimum beside `ChannelMeta` in picker-color.ts. Five homes collapse to one, and `pctReference` removes the 0.4/0.5 ambiguity.

defects.defect: The conversion-graph hover highlight is a value-membership test over the whole graph, so hovering one row lights nodes in every row.
defects.evidence: ColorNutritionLabel.vue:232-240 stores `hoveredPath: string[]` (the hovered row's CONTENTS); :123 tests `hoveredPath.includes(space)` for every node in every row; the row identity is present as `index` at :99 and unused. Measured at ?space=oklch — GRAPH_ROWS [[OKLCh,OKLab],[OKLCh,OKLab,XYZ],[OKLCh,OKLab,XYZ,Lab]]; after hovering row 0: row0 OKLCh filled, OKLab filled; row1 OKLCh filled, OKLab filled, XYZ not; row2 OKLCh filled, OKLab filled, XYZ not, Lab not. 6 nodes lit across 3 rows; 2 are in the hovered row.
defects.mechanism: hover state stored as a value set rather than the hovered row's identity
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe3.mjs — or hover the first Conversion Graph row at http://localhost:9000/#/?space=oklch and observe rows 2 and 3 rendering ragged partial fills (coloured prefix, uncoloured tail).
defects.proposedCure: Split ConversionGraph.vue out of the label and give it `hoveredRow: shallowRef<number | null>`; key the highlight off `rowIndex === hoveredRow`. The leak becomes unwritable.

defects.defect: The section titled "Conversion Graph" renders a hand-authored prose table instead of the library's real conversion topology — a second source of truth for the library's central invariant, unverifiable by any test.
defects.evidence: colorSpaceInfo.ts conversions arrays (e.g. :305-309) are hand-maintained display-string chains. The library owns the actual graph via `convertColor` (@mkbabb/value.js/color), and docs/tranches/V/ARCHITECTURE.md §2's "Total conversion anchor" column specifies every space's real route (prophoto-rgb: "encoded ProPhoto RGB ↔ XYZ D50 ↔ frozen D50/D65 Bradford pair ↔ XYZ D65"). Because the table is authored, it is 5 spaces short and renders RGB→Kelvin→HSL→Hex for Display P3 (see L-1's probe output).
defects.mechanism: documentation of a computed relation duplicated as authored data, with nothing binding the two
defects.reproduction: NONE beyond L-1's probe, which shows the authored graph diverging from truth for every uncovered space.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `conversions` from the content record and derive the route from the library — an exported `conversionRoute(from, to): readonly SpaceId[]` beside convertColor, or ARCHITECTURE §2's anchor chains promoted to exported data. A graph that cannot disagree with the converter is correct for all 17 spaces for free.

defects.defect: Every conversion row mounts a fully-wired but entirely empty tooltip — portal, popper, dismissable layer, glass overlay recipe and ARIA role=tooltip with zero content — and `class="contents"` deletes the box the glass recipe paints into.
defects.evidence: ColorNutritionLabel.vue:139-140 `<TooltipContent class="contents w-64 p-2 text-small"></TooltipContent>` — no children, no slot. Measured after hover: `[data-reka-popper-content-wrapper]` text="" rect 0×0 at (943,902); `[data-state="delayed-open"][data-surface="glass"][data-material="overlay"]` class "… glass-reveal glass-floating …" text="" **display: contents**; `[role="tooltip"]` text="". Also 3 `TooltipProvider` instances measured on the oklch plate — the provider is instantiated inside the v-for at :97-101 where the primitive's contract is one common-ancestor provider. `colorSpaceInfo[space].notes` is authored for all 13 covered spaces and rendered nowhere.
defects.mechanism: a design-system primitive mounted for an empty payload, plus a per-instance display override defeating a root-level glass recipe (edict 5)
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe2.mjs — hover any Conversion Graph row and inspect the portalled subtree.
defects.proposedCure: Either render `notes` into the TooltipContent, drop `class="contents"` so glass-ui's overlay can paint, and hoist ONE TooltipProvider above the v-for; or remove the four Tooltip* imports and the wrapper entirely. Shipping an ARIA-announced empty popper is the worst of the three.

defects.defect: Three type escapes, one proven unnecessary by compiler run and two curable by a signature change rather than a cast.
defects.evidence: ColorNutritionLabel.vue:160 `(currentColorSpaceInfo.industries as any).join(", ")` while :154 `currentColorSpaceInfo.applications.join(", ")` is uncast. Proof — `tsc --noEmit --ignoreConfig --strict --target ES2022 --module esnext --moduleResolution bundler probe.ts` over a file asserting all three, output: only `probe.ts(13,14): error TS2322: Type 'readonly ["RGB","XYZ"] | …' is not assignable to type 'string[]'.` Both `.join` lines type-check clean; the `as any` at :160 is cruft. The `conversions` error is a readonly/mutable mismatch, matching :111 `setHoveredPath(path as any)` and :123 `space as string`.
defects.mechanism: casts used to silence a variance mismatch that belongs in the handler signature
defects.reproduction: cd scratchpad/tsprobe && node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit --ignoreConfig --strict --target ES2022 --module esnext --moduleResolution bundler probe.ts
defects.proposedCure: Delete the :160 cast. Change `setHoveredPath(path: readonly string[])` and `hoveredPath = shallowRef<readonly string[]>([])`; the :111 and :123 casts then vanish. (Subsumed by L-7's ConversionGraph split.)

defects.defect: `ink.ts` — which the subject imports — mixes three concepts in one module and carries a hand-copied duplicate of glass-ui's private theme literals, kept alive as the jsdom branch of a live-probed path.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/ink.ts, 174 lines: (a) universal colour science `contrastInkFor` :158-173, pure, built on the library's own safeAccentColor, zero Vue/DOM; (b) glass-ui's theme values hand-copied — PRODUCER_TINTS :25-28 `card: {light:"hsl(30 85% 96%)", dark:"hsl(26 22% 17%)"}`, RUNG_ALPHA, FLOATING_TINT_L, WELL_FOREGROUND_FRACTION; (c) the demo's surface model. Measured in sync TODAY: `--card` computes to `light-dark(hsl(30 85% 96%), hsl(26 22% 17%))`, `--foreground` to `light-dark(hsl(24 10% 10%), hsl(30 14% 90%))` — identical strings. useContrastSafeColor.ts:225-232 records that this duplication already shipped a contrast failure once: "the light-scheme profile trigger certified against the model's 0.90 while the REAL band composited 0.75 — 3.59:1 measured". The live path works in a real browser (probe measured --glass-bg-resting → color(srgb 0.994 0.96 0.926 / 0.65)), so the static model is reachable only under jsdom.
defects.mechanism: a second implementation of a producer's values retained for the test environment — the canonical dual-path shape (edict 2)
defects.reproduction: NONE for a live wrong render (measured in sync). node scratchpad/probe2.mjs shows the token/literal comparison; the historical failure is cited in-tree.
defects.proposedCure: Split ink.ts three ways: promote `contrastInkFor` into @mkbabb/value.js/color beside safeAccentColor (it is library work); ask glass-ui to export its rung tints/alphas as data so the demo reads rather than copies them (edict 4 relay); leave only the demo's InkSurface model behind. Bind the static model to the live probe with a test, or delete it and let jsdom consumers skip.

defects.defect: The authored `hex` record is dead data — `resolveColorSpace` maps hex→rgb before the lookup, so the entry can never render in either of its two consumers.
defects.evidence: colorSpaceInfo.ts:313-332 authors a full hex record (own definition, created 1996, components ["Red (00-FF)","Green (00-FF)","Blue (00-FF)"]). ColorNutritionLabel.vue:211 applies resolveColorSpace() BEFORE the lookup; color-model.ts:32-34 maps "hex"→"rgb". The only other consumer, ConsoleRail.vue:173-174 `(colorSpaceInfo as any)[space]`, likewise receives the already-resolved space (useColorPipeline.ts:113-115). Live probe at ?space=hex: trigger "Hex"; definition = CIE RGB's; components "Red 0 to 255" — the authored "Red (00-FF)" never appears.
defects.mechanism: computation-space resolution applied to a content lookup — the display space and the compute space collapsed into one variable
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe.mjs, or open http://localhost:9000/#/?space=hex&color=%238a2be2 and read the About pane.
defects.proposedCure: Key content off `selectedColorSpace` (the DisplayColorSpace) and computation off `resolveColorSpace(...)` — the two questions separate, which is precisely what the DisplayColorSpace type was introduced to express. With L-1's exhaustive `Record<SpaceId | "hex", SpaceNote>` the hex row becomes reachable and type-required.

defects.defect: Two home/idiom nits: the 334-line pedagogical prose table is homed in color-session rather than the lattice's `shared/content/`, and provider-tolerance conventions contradict each other inside one feature.
defects.evidence: colorSpaceInfo.ts (334 lines of authored prose — notes, applications, industries) sits in color-session/, whose ARCHITECTURE §1 charter is "active color/specimen, editing target, accent/ink and action context"; the lattice's exact home is `shared/content/  # deliberately authored typed pedagogical snippets`. ColorNutritionLabel.vue:188 `inject(CSS_COLOR_KEY)!` vs ColorSpaceSelector.vue:142 `inject(COLOR_MODEL_KEY, null)` with an explicit "a future host outside any provider renders … rather than crashing" rationale — two opposite conventions in one feature. ColorNutritionLabel.vue:182-183 splits one module across two import statements against the repo idiom (picker-color.ts:22-26).
defects.mechanism: content misfiled as domain state; ad-hoc per-site provider-tolerance policy
defects.reproduction: NONE (structural).
defects.proposedCure: Move the table to demo/shared/content/color-space-notes.ts with M-2's typed shape. Pick one provider-tolerance convention feature-wide and assert it — this becomes load-bearing the moment About becomes the standalone /about route ARCHITECTURE §1 requires, since Picker is then no longer an ancestor. Merge the split import into one statement with inline `type`.

defects.defect: Stale published-surface prose: a local `debounce` copy is justified by a root barrel and a library export that neither exist in 4.0.0.

Measured: `node -e "const p=require('./package.json'); console.log('main',p.main,'rootExport',JSON.stringify(p.exports['.']))"` → `main undefined rootExport undefined` (7 subpath keys, no "."); `grep -rn "export function debounce\|export const debounce" src/` → no output.
defects.mechanism: a comment describing a public surface that was removed without the comment following
defects.reproduction: NONE (structural). Adjacent to the subject — AboutPane's sibling useColorUrl.ts:8 consumes it; not on ColorNutritionLabel's import path.
defects.proposedCure: Correct or delete the rationale. The subpath-only export map is the right design; the prose should say so rather than cite a barrel that would throw ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/scenes/atmosphere/AuroraPane.vue (area: scenes)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id claude-opus-5[1m]; the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with, declared not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: C-1 — the dark-scheme aurora field is still light-band because the demo asserts (useAtmosphere.ts:233-236) that the atoms door "ships no scheme/lBand", while glass-ui 7.0.0 ships BOTH `lightnessScheme` and `lBand` on `AuroraAtomsBase` and a three-line probe proves them reachable through the demo's own resolver (field mean L 0.66 -> 0.30, landing exactly the [0.18,0.42] luminous-dark band glass-ui's doc names). AuroraPane, the declared "≤7-knob consumer-facing surface", exposes neither. The result is visible in the audit's own screenshots: safari-desktop-light/atmosphere.png and safari-desktop-dark/atmosphere.png share an identical salmon field — precisely "a washed-pale salmon field with dark cards floating on it", which the producer doc-comment names as "the dark-leg defect" this atom exists to cure. Cure is already in the tree and collapses a duplicated derive path (the separate scheme-banded deriveAurora at useAtmosphere.ts:237-247) rather than adding one.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable (verdict DEFECTIVE), but the report carries a 9-item negative-proof section so the defects are not confused with the whole: (1) AuroraPane is fully declarative — no rAF, listeners, observers, timers, async or cleanup surface, so the PRM-RAF / leaked-listener / missing-cleanup classes are structurally absent; (2) no defineModel, ValueUnit, stableHue, parseCssColor, WebGL or reka-ui pointer-capture surface in the file; (3) the parse-crash class does not reach here — all 6 harmonies x 6 boundary seeds (#000000, #ffffff, achromatic #808080, oklch(0 0 0), oklch(1 0 0)) gave malformed/throwing = 0; (4) the strip is NOT palette-blind — 6-of-6 pairwise-distinct strips on two chromatic seeds, confirmed in the live DOM; (5) the SelectItem #description slot is real and renders (6/6 options carry a painted 41.9x16.4px strip); (6) the strip recompute is 0.556 ms for all six candidates and SelectContent genuinely unmounts when closed (forceMount count 0), so the "zero rest cost" claim holds; (7) Reset does not clobber the picker seed and the module-level default is never aliased (structuredClone at both sites); (8) zero page errors / console errors / horizontal overflow on /#/atmosphere across all four real-Safari matrices; (9) verbatimModuleSyntax honoured on all four type-only imports, zero nameless buttons on the route, focus returns to the trigger on Escape.

defects.defect: The dark-scheme atmosphere field stays in the light band because the demo carries a stale claim that glass-ui's atoms door ships no `lightnessScheme`/`lBand`; both ARE shipped at 7.0.0 and reachable, and AuroraPane — the atoms tuning surface — exposes neither.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/aurora/composables/atoms.d.ts declares `lightnessScheme?: "light"|"dark"` and `lBand?: readonly [number,number]` on AuroraAtomsBase. Contradicted by demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphere.ts:233-236 ("the atoms door ships no scheme/lBand (GAP-L2 ...) — that half rides packet P1"). Probe: `npx vite-node probe4.mts` -> `no scheme mean L = 0.6600 (0.500,0.607,0.713,0.820)` / `lightnessScheme dark = 0.3000 (0.180,0.260,0.340,0.420)` / `lBand [0.18,0.42] = 0.3000` / `REACHABLE at the atoms door? true true`. Visual: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/atmosphere.png vs .../safari-desktop-dark/atmosphere.png show an identical salmon->pink field; only the card plate darkens. AuroraPane.vue:97-106 (SECTIONS) and :117-180 (enum rows) expose no lightness knob; aurora-atoms.ts:53-71 carries neither key.
defects.mechanism: Stale producer-capability fact frozen in a consumer comment; the Glass 7 adoption (W44) re-verified the build, never the claims. Consumer hand-maintains a duplicate of a producer union with no drift detector.
defects.reproduction: npx vite-node with resolveCalibratedAtmosphere({...DEFAULT_AURORA_ATOMS, seed:'oklch(0.66 0.16 28)', lightnessScheme:'dark'}) — mean palette L moves 0.66 -> 0.30. Or open http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere in a dark-scheme context and compare the field to light: identical.
defects.proposedCure: Feed `lightnessScheme` from useGlobalDark's `isDark` at the ONE place the field is resolved (useAtmosphere.ts:170). That makes the separate scheme-banded ground derive at useAtmosphere.ts:237-247 — which exists only because the field could not be banded — collapse into the same source: two derive paths become one. The scheme is shell state, not a knob; AuroraPane gains a band knob only if the owner wants it tunable.

defects.defect: The harmony PreviewStrip lies about the field it previews: the strip resolver omits the P9-R3 derive-seam guarantee that the painted field goes through, so the strip diverges by up to |dL| = 0.06 OKLCh in half the seed space — violating the O-14 byte-identity truth law the module's own header states.
defects.evidence: aurora-harmony-stops.ts:2-13 states the law; :38 calls only `resolveCalibratedAtmosphere({...atoms, harmony}).palette`. The painted field is `guaranteeSeamOffset(resolveCalibratedAtmosphere(...), seed)` — useAtmosphere.ts:92-110, :170, :179-183. Live: `node live3.mjs` at http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere?space=oklch&color=oklch(0.5%200.16%2010) -> STRIP rgb [[90,23,98],[148,35,92],[192,71,67],[211,125,54]] vs GROUND (--saved-bg-*) rgb [[105,39,112],[165,52,106],[210,87,81],[228,140,71]] — IDENTICAL? false. Extent, verbatim guaranteeSeamOffset over a 14x5 seed grid x 4 harmonies (`npx vite-node probe3.mts`): `strip != painted in 140 / 280 cases; max |dL| = 0.0600`.
defects.mechanism: A truth function separated from its referent: P9-R3 landed the seam guarantee in the provider and the strip module was never re-pointed. The unit oracle compares the strip to the same un-offset function it calls, so it is structurally blind.
defects.reproduction: Navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere?space=oklch&color=oklch(0.5%200.16%2010), open the Harmony select, read the selected row's `data-stops` and compare to document.documentElement.style --saved-bg-0..3. They differ by ~15 rgb units per channel.
defects.proposedCure: The seam guarantee IS the field resolver, not a decoration. Export one `resolveAtmosphereField(atoms)` from boot/atmosphere-calibration.ts composing resolveCalibratedAtmosphere ∘ guaranteeSeamOffset; make useAtmosphere and aurora-harmony-stops both consume it. One resolver, two consumers — the shape the O-14 palettes-ramp leg already uses.

defects.defect: The Zones slider hardcodes max: 6 on a producer ceiling that lifted to 8 at Glass 7, blocking two of three newly-reachable steps and a standing owner mandate; the justifying comment asserts a producer fact that is false at the consumed dist.
defects.evidence: AuroraPane.vue:103 `{ key: "zones.count", label: "Zones", min: 1, max: 6, step: 1 }`. aurora-atoms.ts:35-40 justifies it as `MAX_NUCLEI = 6 ... atom-UNREACHABLE at the consumed dist`. Contradicted: `grep -n "define MAX_NUCLEI" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/aurora.js` -> `128:#define MAX_NUCLEI 8`, `402:#define MAX_NUCLEI 8`. Probe: `zones.count=6 -> nuclei 6 / 7 -> 7 / 8 -> 8 / 9 -> 8`. The repo's own test already knows: demo/test/glass/aurora-bracket.test.ts:117-119 ("Glass 7 raised the ceiling from 6 -> 8") and asserts clamped.nuclei.length === 8. Blocked mandate quoted at aurora-atoms.ts:34: MANDATE §0.5 "The aurora should have a few more zones".
defects.mechanism: Producer constant hardcoded as a literal in a consumer, with the justification frozen in prose rather than derived from the producer.
defects.reproduction: npx vite-node: resolveCalibratedAtmosphere({...DEFAULT_AURORA_ATOMS, zones:{count:8,arrangement:'scattered'}, seed:'oklch(0.66 0.16 28)'}).nuclei.length === 8. Then drag Zones on http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere — it stops at 6.
defects.proposedCure: The pane should not carry the number. Derive max once from the producer clamp (resolveAtoms({zones:{count:99}}).nuclei.length), or ask glass-ui to export MAX_NUCLEI (a one-const coordination packet). Either way the literal 6 leaves the demo.

defects.defect: `class="h-9"` on the four Select triggers overrides glass-ui's tokenized control height, defeating both the coarse-pointer --ui-scale 1.5 and the --control-floor 2.75rem touch floor: measured 36px where the design system resolves 60px.
defects.evidence: AuroraPane.vue:122,142,156,170 all pass `class="h-9 text-caption min-w-menu"`. glass-ui SelectTrigger ships a `size` prop resolving to `h-(--control-h-sm)` / `h-(--control-h-md)` (dist/select-BcBAyLXA.js). dist/styles/tokens/sizing.css: `--control-h-md: max(calc(2.5rem * var(--ui-scale)), var(--control-floor))`; dist/styles/tokens/light-dark.css: `@media (pointer: coarse) { :root { --ui-scale: 1.5; --control-floor: var(--touch-target, 2.75rem); } }`. Measured, `node live4.mjs` on playwright devices['iPhone 14']: `(pointer:coarse) matches: true`, `--ui-scale: 1.5`, `--control-floor: 2.75rem`, and all four triggers `{"h":36,...,"cls":"h-9"}` — 36px vs the resolved 60px, a 40% shortfall and below 44px touch guidance. `text-caption` is likewise a real bridged utility (glass-ui/dist/styles/theme/bridges.css: --text-caption: var(--type-caption)) overriding the trigger's own text-dropdown rung.
defects.mechanism: Per-instance override of a root-level tokenized knob (owner edict 5), x4 elements x2 properties; the override silently disables a responsive token the producer authored so consumers would not hand-size controls.
defects.reproduction: node live4.mjs (playwright, devices['iPhone 14'], goto /#/atmosphere): every .aurora-row button measures height 36 while getComputedStyle(:root) reports --ui-scale 1.5 and --control-floor 2.75rem. The visual REPORT's 24px tap-target threshold reports these as clean.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `h-9` and `text-caption`. If the smaller register is genuinely wanted that is `size="sm"` — the shipped prop, which still honours scale and floor.

defects.defect: The four enum-row labels ride the raw `--muted-foreground` token this repo already condemned twice on the same pane, measuring 3.56:1 in the light scheme at 16.4px — below WCAG 1.4.3's 4.5:1 — while the sibling population on the identical plate measures 13.52:1.
defects.evidence: AuroraPane.vue:194-200 `.aurora-row-label { ... color: var(--muted-foreground); }`. Already ruled on: demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:24-29 ("never raw --muted-foreground, which measured 4.29:1 on the TRUE header ground") and demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:190-206 (T.W8 boot-A re-inks the config population to the certified --ink-muted rung). Measured, `node live5.mjs` (o18-census composite model): LIGHT — all four labels rgb(112,89,66) at fontSize 16.4px, ratio 3.56 (BELOW 4.5:1); sibling .config-console .configurator-row label rgb(28,25,23) ratio 13.52. DARK — 6.12 (passes).
defects.mechanism: Hand-rolled surface bypassing the design system's certified ink rung; no census leg covers .aurora-row-label (the only e2e visiting the route selects .config-console .configurator-row), so it has ridden every close.
defects.reproduction: node live5.mjs against http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere with colorScheme 'light': the four .aurora-row-label elements composite to 3.56:1 against the pane plate. Caveat stated in the report: the composite model is a faithful re-implementation of o18-contrast-census's censusElement, not that function itself; the RELATIVE 13.52 vs 3.56 split on one plate is model-independent.
defects.proposedCure: The certified --ink-muted rung, exactly as the sibling took. Better: stop hand-authoring the row label at all — the C-7 cure deletes this CSS block entirely.

defects.defect: Vacuous gate: no test mounts AuroraPane, no test names any of its four controls, and the one oracle that claims to hold its truth law compares the strip to the same function the strip calls — so the oracle's verdict is inverted with respect to the law.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "Palette harmony|Zone arrangement|Painterly medium|Motion register|aurora-row" e2e/ test/ demo/test/` -> no matches. `grep -rn AuroraPane test/ demo/test/ e2e/` -> only prose in comments. The only e2e visiting the route (e2e/smoke/oracles/o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:929, :1164) censuses `.config-console .configurator-row` — the parent's rows. demo/test/glass/aurora-bracket.test.ts:165-184 compares auroraHarmonyStops(atoms,h) to resolveCalibratedAtmosphere({...atoms,h}).palette — the same function the strip calls, structurally blind to the seam offset of C-2.
defects.mechanism: A law stated in prose in three places and enforced against the wrong side of the seam; a component whose entire DOM surface is untested.
defects.reproduction: Five named mutations that keep vitest (1600+) and every e2e GREEN: M1 swap the Medium/Motion @update:model-value handlers (AuroraPane.vue:155 <-> :169); M2 delete the whole default-slot div (lines 118-180), removing all four controls; M3 SECTIONS[0].defs[2].max 6 -> 1; M4 delete guaranteeSeamOffset from useAtmosphere.ts:170 or set DERIVE_SEAM_FLOOR = 0.5 — GREEN, and the O-14 strip test gets MORE correct because the divergence it cannot see disappears; M5 make setHarmony a no-op.
defects.proposedCure: One Playwright leg on /#/atmosphere that reads each option's `data-stops` (PreviewStrip.vue:44 already stamps them), selects that option, reads --saved-bg-0..3, and asserts equality — the O-14 law as written, measured against the real referent; it fails today. Plus an o18 census leg on .aurora-row-label.

defects.defect: The pane rebuilds the labeled-row primitive its own parent explicitly composes from glass-ui, producing a control column misaligned by 58.7px on desktop and 50.1px on mobile, in a second row grammar sitting outside the sliders' console well.
defects.evidence: AuroraPane.vue:187-192 hand-rolls `.aurora-row { display:flex; justify-content:space-between }` with no label column. Measured, `node live2.mjs` at 1440x900: trigger left edges 318.1 / 365.1 / 306.4 / 306.4 -> SPREAD = 58.7px; widths 897.9 / 850.9 / 909.6 / 909.6 -> SPREAD 58.7px. Mobile (live4.mjs): SPREAD = 50.1px. Visible in shots/safari-desktop-light/atmosphere.png — 'Analogous', 'Scattered', 'Smooth', 'Drifting' each start at a different x. The parent states the broken law at ConfigSliderPane.vue:6-10: 'uses ConfiguratorRow for each labeled row so the demo composes the existing glass-ui surface rather than rebuilding the row primitive'. Compounding: the enum rows render via <slot/> at ConfigSliderPane.vue:110, OUTSIDE the .console-well at :118-122.
defects.mechanism: Hand-rolled surface where a shipped primitive exists (owner edicts 3 and 4); a 14-line CSS block re-derives ConfiguratorRow worse and carries the alignment and contrast defects with it.
defects.reproduction: node live2.mjs against http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere: [...document.querySelectorAll('.aurora-row')].map(r => r.querySelector('button').getBoundingClientRect().left) -> [318.1, 365.1, 306.4, 306.4].
defects.proposedCure: One transposition that kills C-4, C-5 and C-7 together: render the four enum rows as <ConfiguratorRow :label="…"> — the primitive already imported two files up — inside the same .console-well as the sliders. Grid alignment, certified label ink and tokenized control height all arrive by construction, and .aurora-row / .aurora-row-label are deleted.

defects.defect: Three fallback constants in the read/write helpers disagree with the defaults they shadow — stale survivors of the T-32 and U33 landings — a masking-fallback class the owner forbids.
defects.evidence: AuroraPane.vue:74 `atoms.zones?.arrangement ?? "composed"` (DEFAULT is "scattered", aurora-atoms.ts:56); :76 `atoms.motion ?? "breathing"` (DEFAULT is "drifting", aurora-atoms.ts:62); :82 `const count = atoms.zones?.count ?? 4` (DEFAULT count is 6). Probe output: `DEFAULT arrangement: scattered | AuroraPane fallback: 'composed'` / `DEFAULT motion: drifting | AuroraPane fallback: 'breathing'` / `DEFAULT zones.count: 6 | setArrangement fallback count: 4`. The landings that moved them are documented at aurora-atoms.ts:41-45 and :59-62.
defects.mechanism: Hand-copied literals duplicating a value that lives two lines above in the same file's imports; drift with no detector.
defects.reproduction: NONE — latent/dead today: useAtmosphere.ts:128 seeds every key via structuredClone(DEFAULT_AURORA_ATOMS) and ConfigSliderPane.resetDefaults uses Object.assign, which never deletes. Labelled a dead-path defect. Were `zones` ever absent, changing arrangement would silently drop the count 6 -> 4.
defects.proposedCure: `atoms.harmony ?? DEFAULT_AURORA_ATOMS.harmony` etc. — one source of truth, already imported; no hand-copied literal survives.

defects.defect: The pane's three slider thumbs are 12px wide in every matrix, failing WCAG 2.5.8's 24x24 minimum; the coarse-pointer hit-area cure in the parent extends only the block axis, so mobile fixes height (24 -> 44) and leaves width at 12.
defects.evidence: AuroraPane.vue:97-106 defines the three rows. Measured, `node live2.mjs`: `{"label":"Colour Energy","w":12,"h":24}`, `{"label":"Noise","w":12,"h":24}`, `{"label":"Zones","w":12,"h":24}`. These are 3 of the 7 small-tap-target defects REPORT.json attributes to /#/atmosphere in all four matrices (desktop rows `{"w":12,"h":24,"tag":"span","label":"Colour Energy"}`; mobile `{"w":12,"h":44}`). The half-cure is demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:218-229 — `block-size: max(100%, var(--dock-touch-target, 2.75rem))`, block axis only.
defects.mechanism: A touch-target remediation applied on one axis; shared with ConfigSliderPane and the glass-ui Slider, but AuroraPane owns the three rows.
defects.reproduction: node live2.mjs: [...document.querySelectorAll('[role="slider"]')].map(t => t.getBoundingClientRect()) on http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere -> width 12 for all three. Confirmed independently by the real-Safari matrices in REPORT.json.
defects.proposedCure: Mirror the extension on the inline axis (`inline-size: max(100%, 24px)` on the thumb) where the block-axis one already lives — or, correctly, in glass-ui's Slider as a coordination packet.

defects.defect: `inject(AURORA_ATOMS_KEY)!` with no default is a white-screen trapdoor: the non-null assertion is unchecked and every template expression dereferences the result.
defects.evidence: AuroraPane.vue:42 `const atoms = inject(AURORA_ATOMS_KEY)!;`. Dereferenced at :73-76, :79, :82-83, :90, :93, :111, :132. The white-screen class it re-opens is the one useAtmosphere.ts:122-126 explicitly guards ('a thrown getter dead-faults the reactive effect (the white-screen class inv-N-1 forbids)').
defects.mechanism: Non-null assertion standing in for a default on an injection whose provider is a sibling composable, not a structural parent.
defects.reproduction: NONE today — usePaneRouter.ts:88 is the only mount site and always sits under App.vue's useAtmosphereBoot. Labelled a HYPOTHESIS. It becomes real the moment anyone writes the component test C-6 asks for.
defects.proposedCure: `inject(AURORA_ATOMS_KEY, structuredClone(DEFAULT_AURORA_ATOMS))` — the default is already imported in the same file, so this costs nothing and is not a compat shim.

defects.defect: Two `as unknown as Record<string, unknown>` casts hand the dot-path slider keys an untyped key space, so a mistyped knob path compiles and ships; and the four enum readers are plain functions re-invoked every render rather than computed.
defects.evidence: AuroraPane.vue:111 `:config="(atoms as unknown) as Record<string, unknown>"` and :113 the same for DEFAULT_AURORA_ATOMS. `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` exits 0 with no output — because the casts erase the atom type. ConfigSliderPane.vue:27-33 types SliderDef.key as a bare `string`; writePath at :66-73 walks it unchecked (`cur = cur[segs[i]!] as Record<string, unknown>` then `cur[last] = value`), so an absent intermediate segment throws 'Cannot set properties of undefined'. Also AuroraPane.vue:73-76 — harmony/arrangement/medium/motion as plain functions, against owner edict 7.
defects.mechanism: A type cast at the exact seam where the atom type could have checked the pane's own knob names.
defects.reproduction: NONE for a live crash — the reachable paths all exist today. Static: change SECTIONS[0].defs[2].key from 'zones.count' to 'zones.cont' and vue-tsc still exits 0; the slider silently reads undefined and writes a junk key.
defects.proposedCure: Make SliderDef.key generic over the config type so SECTIONS is checked against AuroraAtoms; both casts disappear. Convert the four readers to `computed`.

defects.defect: An identical-branch ternary that reads as dead code (it is in fact a TS union-narrowing device, and its comment explains a distinction the expression does not make), plus fmt() emitting unpaintable CSS on out-of-domain numbers.
defects.evidence: AuroraPane.vue:90 `atoms.medium = kind === "smooth" ? { kind } : { kind };` — byte-identical branches at runtime; it narrows against the AuroraAtoms medium/interactivity discriminated union declared in glass-ui/dist/components/aurora/composables/atoms.d.ts. Comment at :86-88 explains an `amount` distinction the expression does not make. aurora-harmony-stops.ts:26-28 `v.toFixed(4).replace(/\.?0+$/,"")` probed exhaustively: fmt(0)="0", fmt(1)="1", fmt(100)="100", fmt(0.0001)="0.0001", fmt(-12.5)="-12.5" — total and correct in-domain; fmt(1e21)="1e+21", fmt(NaN)="NaN", fmt(Infinity)="Infinity" emit unpaintable CSS.
defects.mechanism: A narrowing idiom written as a runtime branch; a formatter with no domain guard.
defects.reproduction: npx vite-node probe.mts section P3. The unpaintable cases are unreachable — the resolver clamps L/C/h, and P2 confirmed 0 malformed stops across 6 harmonies x 6 boundary seeds including #000000/#ffffff/achromatic.
defects.proposedCure: Express the narrowing as a typed helper (`mediumAtom(kind): AuroraMediumAtom`) so the union discipline is stated once and the call site reads as one assignment; fix or delete the misleading comment.

result.axis: D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Seat declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-2 — in the component's primary interaction state (the open Select), 193,875 px² of underlying interface reads straight through the menu on desktop (63,889 px² on mobile). The option surface computes at α=0.52 with blur(11px) over 16.4px text on a live chromatic canvas, so "Scattered", "Smooth", "Drifting", "Colour Energy 0.760" and the slider tracks are legible THROUGH the harmony options. Two text runs occupy the same pixels. `/#/atmosphere` is absent from every route list in audit/visual/states.mjs:18, so no capture in this repository had ever held this state open — I captured it (frames/desktop-light-harmony-open.png, frames/mobile-harmony-open.png). Tied for structural weight with D-1 (the atmosphere pane contains zero preview: canvasesInMain=0 at every matrix while the card occupies 52.54% of the desktop viewport and 76.31% of mobile, occluding the only aurora surface — PR-10 and VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §29/§51/§214 all unremedied).
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but these are the checks that came back clean, stated so absence-of-finding is evidence rather than silence: (1) No horizontal overflow at any matrix — documentElement.scrollWidth − clientWidth === 0 at desktop LTR, RTL and 200%-zoom; REPORT.md agrees (`horizontalOverflow — 0`). (2) RTL is structurally correct — frames/rtl.png shows labels mirrored to inline-end, controls to inline-start, footer order reversed, no overflow; the only artefact is a bidi period on the description, which is PaneHeader/content-owned. (3) The 200%-zoom menu FITS — I expected a clip and did not find one: the longest menu (Medium, 7 options) measures h=270 in a 450px viewport, overflowBottom=−153, 7 of 7 options visible, not scrollable. (4) Zero page errors and zero console errors on the route in all four Safari matrices (REPORT.md:126,141,156,171). (5) The harmony strips tell the truth — aurora-harmony-stops.ts:38 resolves through resolveCalibratedAtmosphere, held to a direct recompute by test/preview-chips.test.ts; they are undersized (D-11) but not lying. (6) Edict 6 (animations) CLEAN — the component declares no keyframes, deletes none, hand-rolls no motion; all motion on its surface is producer-owned. (7) Edict 8 (verbatimModuleSyntax) CLEAN — all four type imports are `import type` (AuroraPane.vue:25, :26-31, :34). (8) Edict 1 (no god modules) CLEAN — 201 lines, one concern. (9) Edict 2 (no dual paths) CLEAN — `demo/ui/select` is a single re-export used by all six Select consumers; `grep -rn "SelectTrigger" demo --include="*.vue" | grep glass-ui` returns 0 competing direct imports. (10) VISUAL-CONSTITUTION:104 HELD — the three numeric atoms do ride the one glass-ui ConfiguratorRow axis composition. (11) Reduced motion not born-RED here, per the root's verified raf/1.5s=0 finding. (12) C2 "aurora palette-blind static-Sky" not re-litigated — it is a producer-signature chronic, and D-1 is a distinct, larger defect.

defects.defect: The atmosphere pane renders zero preview surface. Four of its seven knobs (harmony/arrangement/medium/motion) have no read-out anywhere in the component, and the form is stacked on top of the only aurora surface it tunes.
defects.evidence: probe-D.json: canvasesInMain=0 and canvasesInPage=1 in all four matrices (desktop-light, desktop-dark, mobile, zoom-200); cardShareOfViewport = 52.54% (1440x900, cardRect 1042x653.42), 76.31% (mobile 390x664), 53.41% (zoom-200). The one canvas is the app-shell aurora, outside `main`. Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:54 `PR-10 Atmosphere/Blob form acreage exceeds preview → TIGHTEN`; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:29 'Atmosphere/Blob preview area is larger than the form at every desktop size'; :51 'persistent Aurora preview | compact atom essentials plus scroll-confined advanced disclosure | preview, essentials, advanced'; :214 'every select/axis has an observable effect on its live preview'.
defects.mechanism: The route was built as ConfigSliderPane-with-extra-rows — a settings card — where the constitution specifies a preview-dominant instrument. ConfigSliderPane.vue:98-101 hard-codes a `w-full h-full` Card with no stage slot, so the pane could not host a preview even if AuroraPane asked for one.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AuroraPane/probe-D.mjs → out['desktop-light'].acreage.canvasesInMain === 0. Visually: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/atmosphere.png — the aurora is visible only in the margin strip around a card filling the centre of the screen.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition: move /atmosphere from 'a form card over the page ground' to the constitution's preview-dominant composition — a bounded live aurora stage at 66.6666667% of the desktop scene, controls at 33.3333333%, mobile as stage→inspector→action (§3.6). Reorder to preview → essentials (colour energy/noise/zones) → advanced disclosure (harmony/arrangement/medium/motion). This is the only change that can give arrangement/medium/motion the observable effect §214 demands.

defects.defect: The open Select does not occlude what it covers: 193,875 px² of underlying interface is legible through the desktop menu, 63,889 px² through the mobile menu. Two text runs share the same pixels.
defects.evidence: probe-D3.json — desktop overlap by element: aurora-row-label 'Arrangement' 862 px²; control-surface 'Scattered' 30,634; 'Smooth' 32,328; 'Drifting' 32,328; configurator-row 'Colour Energy0.760' 53,808; 'Noise0.500' 43,915 → TOTAL 193,875 px². Mobile totals 63,889 px² across 7 elements incl. 'Zones6'. Surfaces: contentBg oklab(0.955861 0.009528 0.029646 / 0.7488), optionBg oklab(0.915631 0.00547 0.013051 / 0.52), contentBackdrop blur(11px) saturate(1.6), contentOpacity 1. Frames: frames/desktop-light-harmony-open.png, frames/mobile-harmony-open.png — 'Scattered' reads through 'Analogous', the Colour Energy slider track runs across 'Triad'.
defects.mechanism: Two compounding causes. (a) glass-ui's SelectContent/SelectItem surface recipe (α 0.75 / α 0.52 + 11px blur) is tuned for an opaque app background, not for a translucent card over a live chromatic canvas. (b) AuroraPane makes the menu enormous — the trigger is 897.86px wide (D-3), so the menu inherits 889.86px and blankets three sibling rows plus two slider rows instead of being a compact list beside its own row.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AuroraPane/probe-D3.mjs; or open http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere, click the Harmony trigger, and read the text behind the menu.
defects.proposedCure: Demo-side: D-3's cure removes the 890px width inheritance, so the menu stops covering the form. Producer-side this needs a COORDINATION PACKET, not a wave (glass-ui@^7.0.0 is not ours to edit this formation): SelectContent needs a resting opacity, or an opaque scrim beneath the blur, sufficient for content-over-chroma compositions.

defects.defect: Four control rows, three different left edges — a 58.65px ragged spread on desktop, 50.08px on mobile (14.0% of the 358px card).
defects.evidence: probe-D.json desktop-light trigger x: Harmony 318.14, Arrangement 365.06, Medium 306.41, Motion 306.41 → spread 58.65px. Mobile: 115.11 / 155.17 / 105.09 / 105.09 → spread 50.08px on cardW 358. RTL mirrors rather than fixes it — frames/rtl.png shows four chevrons at four different x.
defects.mechanism: AuroraPane.vue:187-192 `.aurora-row { display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; gap:0.75rem }`. space-between anchors the label left and the control right, so each control's inline-start is a function of its label's text length. A label column plus a control column is a grid, not a space-between flex row.
defects.reproduction: node probe-D.mjs → compare out['desktop-light'].rows[*].trigRect.x. Visually: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-mobile-light/atmosphere.png — the four pills form a zig-zag left edge.
defects.proposedCure: Delete .aurora-row entirely and render the enum rows through glass-ui's ConfiguratorRow (the primitive the sibling slider rows in the SAME card already use), which supplies one shared label column.

defects.defect: A hand-rolled labeled-row primitive sits inside the same Card as the glass-ui row primitive its sibling rows use. One card, two row primitives, seven rows split 4/3 between them.
defects.evidence: ConfigSliderPane.vue:21 imports ConfiguratorRow from '@mkbabb/glass-ui/configurator' and :137 renders every slider row through it; that file's own header at :6-10 states the law ('uses ConfiguratorRow for each labeled row so the demo composes the existing glass-ui surface rather than rebuilding the row primitive'). AuroraPane.vue:118-180 then fills that component's default slot with .aurora-row/.aurora-row-label — a second labeled-row primitive. AuroraPane.vue:194-200 is additionally a verbatim five-declaration copy of ConfigSliderPane.vue:237-243 (.config-section-title): same properties, same values, copied not shared.
defects.mechanism: The enum atoms were treated as 'extra controls' needing bespoke markup rather than as peer rows of the same AuroraAtoms door. Owner edicts 3 (KISS, no contrivance) and 4 (glass-ui is the design system) both land here.
defects.reproduction: Read AuroraPane.vue:118-180 and :187-200 against ConfigSliderPane.vue:137-153 and :232-243. The measurable downstream cost is D-3 (raggedness), D-5 (broken spine + two rhythms), D-6 (36px tap rung vs the sibling rows' 44px), D-7 (inert label), D-8 (voice inversion).
defects.proposedCure: Delete .aurora-row, .aurora-row-label and the wrapper div at AuroraPane.vue:118; render the four enum atoms as ConfiguratorRows whose control slot carries the Select. One primitive yields one spine, one container-scaled rhythm, one aligned edge, the coarse-pointer 44px hit rung and the label↔control association for free. Verify first whether ConfiguratorRow wires for/id for a non-slider control; if not, that is a coordination packet.

defects.defect: The card carries two vertical text spines 15px apart and two conflicting rhythms — and the enum rows are the only fixed-metric rows in a container-scaled pane.
defects.evidence: Measured both viewports: desktop cardX 199, auroraLabelX 224, sectionTitleX 239, sliderRowX 239 (Δ=15px); mobile cardX 16, auroraLabelX 33, sectionTitleX 48, sliderRowX 48 (Δ=15px). Rhythm: auroraRowH 36.00 desktop AND 36.00 mobile with gaps [12,12,12]; sliderRowH 60.94 desktop / 77.59 mobile with gaps [6,6]. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:33 (§3.7) 'Spacing is container-scaled from glass-ui tokens. No desktop-tight/mobile-airy fork and no breakpoint pile.'
defects.mechanism: The .console-well begins at x=224 (same inset as the enum block) but adds `padding: 0.75rem 0.875rem` (ConfigSliderPane.vue:189), pushing its contents to 239 — and the enum block never enters the well. Separately, AuroraPane hard-codes `h-9` (AuroraPane.vue:122,142,156,170) where the sibling rows ride `min-block-size: clamp(2rem, 7cqi, 2.625rem)` (ConfigSliderPane.vue:216), and the enum block carries the breakpoint pile `px-4 sm:px-6 pt-2 pb-1` (AuroraPane.vue:118). The looser 12px gap also sits on the SHORTER rows and the tighter 6px gap on the taller ones — optically backwards.
defects.reproduction: node /tmp/.../spine.mjs equivalent, or in the live page evaluate `document.querySelector('.aurora-row-label').getBoundingClientRect().x` vs `document.querySelector('.config-section-title').getBoundingClientRect().x` → 224 vs 239. Visually: shots/safari-desktop-light/atmosphere.png — 'HARMONY' hangs left of 'FIELD' and 'Colour Energy'.
defects.proposedCure: Covered by D-4's cure: rendering the enum rows through ConfiguratorRow inside the same .console-well puts every label on one spine at one container-scaled rhythm, and retires both the h-9 pin and the px-4 sm:px-6 breakpoint fork.

defects.defect: Four style declarations on the Select trigger are dead — the rendered component is not the component that was designed, and nothing says so. Consequence: the selected value of all four controls renders italic sans at the label's own size.
defects.evidence: probe-D2.json.deadDeclarations, read off the live Harmony trigger: classList contains producer `text-dropdown` … then `h-9 text-caption min-w-menu`; typeCaptionToken `clamp(0.75rem, 0.71rem + 0.21vw, 1rem)` → typeCaptionResolvedPx 14.375px, but computedFontSize **16.4px**. selectFontToken '"Fira Code", …, monospace' (foundation.css:371-373 'PROJECT OVERRIDE: monospace fonts for Select and DropdownMenu triggers') vs computedFontFamily '"Plus Jakarta Sans", …, sans-serif'. computedFontStyle **italic**. `max-h-[16rem]` = 256px vs the open menu's measured h 322.28, scrollH===clientH===320, scrollable:false. `min-w-menu` is inert — the producer already applies w-full; measured widths 850.94–909.59 are flex-fill.
defects.mechanism: Per-instance utility classes appended to a producer class list cannot defeat a producer root rule — CSS order, not string order, decides. Owner edict 5 ('style at the shadcn/glass root component level, never per-instance overrides') violated four times, four silent failures. The italic arrives free from the producer and the component accepts it; in this app italic is the pane-DESCRIPTION register (PaneHeader.vue:29 .pane-header-desc), so the row's protagonist wears the voice of explanatory prose and reads as placeholder text.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AuroraPane/probe-D2.mjs → out.deadDeclarations. Visually the italic is unmistakable in all four Safari captures: 'Analogous', 'Scattered', 'Smooth', 'Drifting'.
defects.proposedCure: Delete all four per-instance classes. If a caption rung or mono voice is genuinely wanted on Select triggers, it belongs at the glass-ui root — a coordination packet asking whether `--select-font` is still a live seam in Glass 7 (measured: it is not), and whether the trigger's italic default is intentional.

defects.defect: The visible label is not a label. Clicking 'HARMONY' does nothing: no focus, no open, no pointer affordance.
defects.evidence: probe-D2.json.labelClick — before { expanded:'false', focused:'BODY' }; after clicking .aurora-row-label 'Harmony': { expanded:'false', focused:'BODY', listboxOpen:false, labelCursor:'auto' }. probe-D.json rows: labelTag 'SPAN', labelHasFor false, trigAriaLabelledby null. AuroraPane.vue:120,140,154,168 are bare <span class="aurora-row-label">.
defects.mechanism: The hand-rolled row (D-4) skipped the label association that ConfiguratorRow's `label` prop supplies to the sibling slider rows (ConfigSliderPane.vue:139). A <span> styled exactly like a form label, positioned exactly where one goes, doing none of a form label's work — no for, no aria-labelledby, no click-to-focus, no hit-area contribution. Secondary: the accessible name is a second vocabulary ('Palette harmony' / 'Zone arrangement' / 'Painterly medium' / 'Motion register') against the visible 'HARMONY' / 'ARRANGEMENT' / 'MEDIUM' / 'MOTION' — each contains its visible string so WCAG 2.5.3 is not breached, but two names for one knob is a seat-law defect (PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:70-71).
defects.reproduction: node probe-D2.mjs, or click the word HARMONY at http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere and observe nothing happens.
defects.proposedCure: Covered by D-4: ConfiguratorRow's label prop restores the association, the click target and the pointer affordance. Then collapse the two vocabularies to one name per knob.

defects.defect: Typographic hierarchy is exactly inverted: the leaf control label and the group section title compute byte-identical, while the leaf label and its PEER leaf label differ in family, weight, tracking, case and colour. Label:value size ratio is 1.000 on desktop and 0.667 on mobile — the relation inverts direction between viewports.
defects.evidence: probe-D2.json.voice — .aurora-row-label 'Harmony' (LEAF): Fira Code 16.4px w400 ls 1.64px uppercase rgb(112,89,66). .config-section-title 'Field' (GROUP): Fira Code 16.4px w400 ls 1.64px uppercase rgb(112,89,66) — identical. .configurator-row 'Colour Energy' (PEER LEAF): Plus Jakarta Sans 16.4px w500 ls normal none rgb(28,25,23). Proportion: desktop label 16.4px : value 16.4px = 1.000; mobile label 14px : value 21px = 0.667. Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:15 requires paired rungs at label/headline = 1/√φ ≈ 0.786; :16 'Mobile and desktop use the same source.'
defects.mechanism: AuroraPane.vue:194-200 copies .config-section-title's exact recipe onto a leaf label, so rank information is destroyed. The colour split compounds it: enum labels are muted rgb(112,89,66) while peer slider labels are full-strength rgb(28,25,23), making the four enum rows read as secondary/disabled when all seven are peer atoms of one AuroraAtoms door. The label and value rungs resolve from two different clamps (--type-small vs the producer's trigger size) that cross between 390px and 1440px.
defects.reproduction: node probe-D2.mjs → out.voice. Visually: shots/safari-desktop-light/atmosphere.png — 'HARMONY' and 'FIELD' are indistinguishable; 'HARMONY' and 'Colour Energy' look like different kinds of thing.
defects.proposedCure: D-4's cure gives all seven rows one label voice. Then set the label/value pair from ONE paired clamp so the 1/√φ relation holds at every arm, per PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:15-16, instead of two independently-clamped rungs.

defects.defect: Nothing the pane does survives a reload — including the app's only ambient-motion stop control. The sole export is write-only and silently carries the user's live colour.
defects.evidence: probe-D2.json.persistence = { set: 'Still', afterReload: 'Drifting', persisted: false }. useAtmosphere.ts:128 is `reactive(structuredClone(DEFAULT_AURORA_ATOMS))` with no storage read or write in the chain. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:145 'Continuous Aurora/Blob ambient motion terminates within five seconds or exposes one persistent keyboard-operable still/pause control whose state is announced and remembered'; :99 'Persistent operation state stays with the entity/workspace.'
defects.mechanism: The atoms object is component-lifetime reactive state with no workspace persistence layer. The Motion select IS the app's only still control, but it is route-local (behind a Dock navigation), named 'Motion register' rather than announced as a motion control, and not remembered. The escape hatch — Copy JSON (ConfigSliderPane.vue:88-90) — serialises `config`, which useAtmosphere.ts:132-139 has written the live picker `seed` onto, and no import path exists anywhere in the app.

defects.defect: Non-idiomatic reactivity with a measurable cost: an open Harmony menu performs six full `resolveCalibratedAtmosphere` palette solves per render.

defects.reproduction: NONE measured as a frame-time regression — hypothesis on cost magnitude. The call structure is directly readable at AuroraPane.vue:73-76 and :132.
defects.proposedCure: Replace the four getter functions with `computed`, and memoise the six harmony strips on the atoms identity so they resolve once per atoms change rather than once per render.

defects.defect: Forced-colors behaviour is unproven in both directions; the structural risk is an alpha-only control boundary with no fallback.

defects.reproduction: NONE — HYPOTHESIS. Requires a real Windows High Contrast machine; the Playwright forcedColors emulation is not evidence either way.
defects.proposedCure: Do not born-RED this on emulator evidence. Book a real-HCM verification, and in the meantime give the trigger a non-alpha boundary and an `outline` (not box-shadow) focus indicator at the glass-ui root — the same coordination packet as D-6.

result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the masking fallback at `ColorNutritionLabel.vue:212-214` makes 6 of the 18 selectable color spaces publish ANOTHER space's encyclopedia as authoritative fact. Selecting "Display P3" renders RGB's definition, "Device-dependent", "Varies (typically D65)", "Limited (device-specific)", "Created: 1931" and an RGB-only conversion graph — four falsehoods in a block headed "Basic Information", with the trigger visibly reading Display P3. Probe under `forcedColors: active` shows zero forced-colors adaptation in this subtree: `{"compColor":"oklch(0.519287 0.207684 9.834023)","alertBg":"oklab(0.913299 …)"}`. CAVEAT: WebKit's emulation sets the media query but does not perform real system-color substitution, so the probe proves the ABSENCE of any authored forced-colors rule, not final WHCM pixels; the roster omission is a static verifiable fact against a written policy.
defects.mechanism: Code claims membership in a roster it never joined
defects.reproduction: `grep -n 'data-o18\|data-color-surface' demo/styles/foundation.css` returns nothing in the 680-695 roster; `node scratchpad/CNL-D-probe3.mjs` → `C/forced`, `C/dark-forced`.
defects.proposedCure: Add the color-data node to the tier-1 roster (or give it `data-color-surface`). Better: apply D-3's cure so the color is a FILL, which is precisely what the roster exists to protect.

defects.defect: No document semantics: five anonymous <section>s, five <h2>s under zero <h1>, and a description list written as divs

defects.defect: `defineModel<ColorModel>` gives a read-only presentational leaf a two-way handle on the whole color session, to read one string
